best_feature_set.feature: One-gesture start from anywhere on the watch (and phone)
best_feature_set.description: One tap from a complication, a watchOS 26 Control (Control Center or Smart Stack), the Ultra Action Button, or Double Tap inside the app starts a capture session. The iPhone can start the same session. Watch recording works standalone and offline. Consent defaults are set once on first run, so the daily start is a single tap, not a wizard.
best_feature_set.rationale: One-tap start is the most-praised trait in the watch market scan (Whisper Memos, Just Press Record, Talk Memo), and tap_or_push_to_talk is the second most common feature in the catalog (202/272). watchOS only lets capture begin from a user action in the foreground, so the one thing left to optimise is how cheap that action is. That action is the habit trigger: put the watch on, tap 'Start my day'.

best_feature_set.feature: Zero-loss capture pipeline with visible sync states
best_feature_set.description: Audio goes into small local segments recorded in a journal. A segment is deleted from the watch only after the phone or cloud confirms receipt by hash. The user sees a status ladder (Recording, Queued, Synced, Transcribed, Summarized) with automatic retries instead of silent failure. On the next launch, crash recovery collects any orphaned segments.
best_feature_set.rationale: Recordings that are lost or never transferred are the top complaint across watch apps. Omi lost an 11 h watch session, Voice Memos truncated an hour-long recording to seconds, and Drafts sync broke after a watchOS update. In a capture product, reliability is the product: one silent loss wipes out the trust built by months of good summaries. Granola's explicit sync-with-retry states are the pattern to copy.
exemplars: Omi (open-source platform & SDK) - anti-exemplar, 11 h watch loss

best_feature_set.feature: Interruption-aware sessions with honest coverage
best_feature_set.description: When a call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app ends capture, the app closes the open segment with a reason, records a gap, and gives one haptic 'Tap to resume' nudge. Summaries and answers know about the gaps ('not recorded 10:42-10:55') and never imply the record is complete.
best_feature_set.rationale: An interrupted watch recording cannot be resumed from the background (Apple Frameworks Engineer, forum 750432). Granola cannot resume interrupted watch recordings, and Voicenotes users report it 'stopped recording mid-session'. Users forgive a gap they were told about; they do not forgive finding one later. Answers that know the coverage also can't confidently invent what happened during unrecorded periods.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind) - pauses during calls/FaceTime

best_feature_set.feature: Verifiable record: full transcript, me-vs-others, cited summaries, short audio window
best_feature_set.description: Each conversation gets a full timestamped transcript that separates at least the wearer from everyone else. Every summary line and action item links to its transcript span. Audio stays playable for a short, user-set verification window (for example 7-30 days) and is then deleted automatically.
best_feature_set.rationale: Siri Recap deliberately ships summaries only: no transcript, no speakers, 7-day retention. That is the clearest opening for a third party. Bee deletes audio, so users cannot check summaries that hallucinate or that picked up the TV. The Earshot notes conclude that accuracy failures hurt trust more than missing features, and diarization is weak almost everywhere. Citations turn 'the AI said so' into 'here is where they said it'.
exemplars: Rev (AI Notetaker and Voice Recorder app)

best_feature_set.feature: Moment bookmarks
best_feature_set.description: One press while recording flags the last ~60 seconds. Flagged spans are pinned to the top of the day's output and weighted more heavily in summaries and action-item extraction.
best_feature_set.rationale: Ambient capture is mostly noise: a six-month Limitless user judged about 10% of 10 GB valuable. A bookmark is the cheapest possible signal of intent, it needs no transcription on the watch, and it is the most repeated hardware affordance in the category. It also gives the user an active part, an investment, in an otherwise passive product.

best_feature_set.feature: Commitments and action items sent to the user's own tools, with approval
best_feature_set.description: Extract to-dos, promises ('I'll send it Friday'), dates and follow-ups. One tap sends an item to Reminders, Calendar, Things, Todoist or Notion. In v1 nothing is created without the user's approval.
best_feature_set.rationale: Action items are what people act on and pay for (135/272 products), and automatic routing is one of the best-loved features in the watch scan. Building yet another task inbox competes with the user's own system; feeding that system creates daily value without asking for a new habit.

best_feature_set.feature: Consent and bystander controls as first-class UX
best_feature_set.description: An audible and haptic start cue plus the system mic indicator. One-tap Pause (with a timer) and Stop. Consent reminders that depend on jurisdiction (all-party US states, the EEA, Germany). A wearer-only retention mode that is the default where the law is strict. Scheduled audio deletion. Explicit opt-in before any third-party AI processing.
best_feature_set.rationale: App Review requires it (guidelines 2.5.14 and 5.1.2(i)), and the legal climate is tightening: Brewer v. Otter.ai, Subia v. Meta, and EDPB Statement 01/2026, which says consent obtained after recording is invalid. Germany's §201 StGB carries criminal penalties. It is also a retention feature: the Limitless user stopped wearing it in social settings, and a Bee user's partner banned it at home. Apple has set the bar with a chime even on silent, opt-in and short retention.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Search and Ask over history, with citations and 'not recorded' honesty (phone/web)
best_feature_set.description: Full-text and semantic search across transcripts, plus natural-language questions. Every answer cites transcript spans, and when the relevant period wasn't captured the answer says so instead of guessing.
best_feature_set.rationale: Being able to find things later is the payoff that justifies wearing a mic (ask_ai_over_history 112/272, searchable_memory 111/272). The long-term Limitless verdict was 'a fancy transcription service with a mediocre search', so answers have to be cited and aware of what wasn't recorded to earn repeat use.
exemplars: Rev (AI Notetaker and Voice Recorder app)

best_feature_set.feature: Honest battery and storage budget
best_feature_set.description: Drain is measured per watch model and profile and shown as projected hours. Recording stops automatically at a user-set battery floor (default 15%) or when storage runs low, and a lower-bitrate profile kicks in under Low Power Mode. Marketing promises 'your workday', not 24/7.
best_feature_set.rationale: Battery uncertainty is a top-10 complaint, and almost every figure in the category is a vendor claim. Series 11/12 is rated 24 h for everything, and the research estimates about 10-14 h of continuous recording on Series 11/12 and 8-11 h on SE 3 (low confidence). Watch apps outside the catalog (Tiro, Wave, Hedy) already auto-stop at battery thresholds. A watch that dies at 5 pm fails at being a watch and kills the habit.
exemplars: Pebble Index 01 (states a fixed battery life plainly)

best_feature_set.feature: Open export and agent access
best_feature_set.description: Bulk export of transcripts (Markdown/JSON), summaries and audio (AAC) with a documented schema, plus a read-only MCP endpoint and API so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can query the user's memory with permission.
best_feature_set.rationale: Users' memories die with the company: Humane bricked its devices, and Limitless turned off capture and deleted regional data within two weeks of being acquired. Agent access is now table stakes (Granola, Omi, Pebble, Monologue, Screenpipe), and 'no bulk export' is a recorded Voicenotes complaint.

best_feature_set.feature: Evening recap on the wrist: 'today in three lines'
best_feature_set.description: After processing, a Smart Stack widget or complication shows today's coverage (hours captured, gaps), the 1-3 commitments that matter, and one recalled detail. A tap opens a short list; full detail stays on the phone. The phone also gets a weekly version.
best_feature_set.rationale: This is the variable reward of the habit loop, and it fills the 'can't review on the wrist' gap: today's watch apps only capture. The best praise for Siri Recap was that it surfaced a detail the family had forgotten. Daily recaps are common on dedicated wearables but rare on the wrist.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Commitment tracking with rare, well-timed nudges
best_feature_set.description: Track promises by person and due date. Nudge only when a deadline is near or just before meeting that person, behind a value-of-information gate (default at most about 2 a day). Delivery is passive by default and the user can tune it.
best_feature_set.rationale: Remembering what you promised is a high-value job: it is the whole pitch of Luna/Samantha, and Halliday checks commitments in the lens. Unwanted proactivity is the fastest route to an uninstall, though: Friend's unprompted texts came across as intrusive, and Omi was called a 'micromanager' and removed its automatic reflections.

best_feature_set.feature: Briefs before you meet someone
best_feature_set.description: Before a calendar event, or on request, show the open items, promises and last decisions from earlier conversations with the same people.
best_feature_set.rationale: This turns past capture into future value and is the strongest repeat-use loop in meeting tools. It also justifies keeping transcripts beyond Apple's 7 days.

best_feature_set.feature: Context-triggered start prompts and pause zones
best_feature_set.description: The app can't start itself, so the phone uses calendar events and places to send a timely 'Tap to start', or 'You're home - pause?'. RelevanceKit brings the right widget forward in the Smart Stack. Users can define places such as home, the therapist's office or the gym where the app suggests pausing.
best_feature_set.rationale: Users will expect Siri Recap's scheduling by time or place. Because the platform forbids starting capture in the background, a prompt is the honest equivalent. Pause zones protect social acceptability, which is the first thing to erode.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Coverage Apple leaves out: older watches, more languages, longer retention
best_feature_set.description: Support every watch that runs watchOS 27 (Series 9+, Ultra 2+, SE 3), with a watchOS 26 fallback. Transcribe in more than English, and let the user choose retention.
best_feature_set.rationale: Siri Recap needs a Series 12 or Ultra 4 plus an iPhone 16 or later, works in English only, is not in the EU, and keeps results for 7 days. That leaves out most of the installed base and most of the world. The EU gap comes with EDPB risk.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind) - benchmark/gap

best_feature_set.feature: Media and noise filtering; conversation boundary detection
best_feature_set.description: Drop TV, podcasts and music; split the day into separate conversations so recaps read as events, not a stream.
best_feature_set.rationale: The Verge found that Bee treated TV and songs as conversation and leaked muted periods into summaries. Summarising the television is a trust killer.

best_feature_set.feature: Ask from the wrist
best_feature_set.description: Raise, tap and ask 'what did Dana say about the launch date?'. The watch shows a one- or two-sentence answer with a citation chip and a haptic, and deep-links to the phone.
best_feature_set.rationale: Searching or asking your memories from the watch is a named unmet need. Petey's 3.8 rating shows open-ended chat on the wrist is hard, so keep it scoped to the user's own memory and short. Ship it only after capture is reliable.
exemplars: Petey - AI Chat for Watch (formerly WatchGPT)

best_feature_set.feature: Unmetered capture and transcription; pay for synthesis (plus a local-only mode)
best_feature_set.description: The free tier never meters capture or on-device transcripts. The paid tier, priced against a $69.99-$99/yr anchor, buys cloud synthesis, commitments, briefs, long retention and multi-device sync. An optional local-only, no-account mode is available.
best_feature_set.rationale: Subscription fatigue is real (Bee Pro $11.99/mo, Omi Pro $29.99/mo), and minute caps (Plaud's 300 free min/mo) punish always-on use. On-iPhone SpeechAnalyzer makes transcription close to free at the margin. Pocket, Comulytic and HiDock already market unlimited free transcription, Pebble markets 'no subscription', and Just Press Record at $6.99 one-time is still loved.

best_feature_set.feature: Agentic follow-ups with approval (emails, recap messages, CRM fields, documents)
best_feature_set.description: Draft and, after approval, send follow-ups or update systems from a conversation.
best_feature_set.rationale: High value for professionals, but the potential damage from a wrong action is large and trust has to be earned first. Plaud, TicNote and Comu already fight over this ground.

best_feature_set.feature: Desktop and online-meeting capture into the same memory
best_feature_set.description: Botless Mac/PC capture of Zoom, Meet and Teams calls, merged into the same timeline.
best_feature_set.rationale: This is a different job in a crowded field (44 meeting notetakers in the catalog). Import from or integrate with those tools before building it.

best_feature_set.feature: Phone-call capture
best_feature_set.description: Bring the user's phone calls into the timeline.
best_feature_set.rationale: iOS already records calls natively and notifies all participants, and the consent rules are complex. Importing from iOS call recordings is the cheaper route.
exemplars: Apple Voice Memos & Notes audio transcription (Apple Intelligence)

best_feature_set.feature: Health, place and calendar context on the timeline
best_feature_set.description: Tag conversations with place, calendar event, and optionally sleep, heart rate and stress.
best_feature_set.rationale: Useful enrichment that improves recall and briefs, but not the core job.

best_feature_set.feature: Context templates and custom summary styles
best_feature_set.description: Different output shapes for 1:1s, lectures, client visits and journaling.
best_feature_set.rationale: Power users love it (Plaud's 10,000+ templates, AudioPen styles), but it adds configuration cost before the core loop is proven.

best_feature_set.feature: Live captions and translation
best_feature_set.description: Real-time captions or translation relayed to the wrist or earbuds.
best_feature_set.rationale: Real accessibility value, but the watch has no speech recognition, and a phone round trip costs latency and battery.

best_feature_set.feature: People and project pages; shared team memory
best_feature_set.description: Auto-built pages per person and project, and optional shared team memory.
best_feature_set.rationale: Strong when there is a lot of history, but it needs months of data and adds multi-party consent problems.

best_feature_set.feature: Optional companion mic hardware
best_feature_set.description: Pair a clip or ring mic for better pickup and battery.
best_feature_set.rationale: Dedicated multi-mic devices probably out-hear a wrist mic. A partnership is cheaper than building hardware.

minimal_watch_set.feature: One-tap 'Start my day' with consent cue
minimal_watch_set.description: Start a capture session from a complication, a Control (Control Center or Smart Stack), the Ultra Action Button, or Double Tap on the app's start screen. Starting plays a short chime and a haptic and shows an unmistakable Recording state. Consent and jurisdiction defaults are set once on first run.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: An app that must be started by hand every day only becomes a habit if the trigger is nearly effortless, and one-tap start is the most-praised trait of watch recorders. Capture can only begin from a user action in the foreground, so this is the only way into 'always running'. The cue meets guideline 2.5.14 and sets bystanders' expectations.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: A WidgetKit accessory complication and a watchOS 26 Control whose intent opens the app. Controls run in the widget extension and capture must start in the foreground, so they launch the app rather than record. Assign the Control to the Ultra Action Button. The Start button uses .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) for Double Tap (S9 and later, including SE 3; not in Low Power Mode or wrist-down). Enable the audio background mode. On Start, call AVAudioSession setCategory(.record) and setActive(true) once per session, then play a chime and a WKInterfaceDevice haptic; the system shows the orange mic indicator. Do not use the Digital Crown double-press, which belongs to Live Rewind on Series 12 and Ultra 4.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Durable, VAD-gated background capture in a crash-safe segment journal
minimal_watch_set.description: Once started, the mic stays open in the background with the wrist down. Only speech is encoded, written in 2-minute segments that are each closed, hashed and journaled, so a crash or reboot loses at most the open segment.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: This is the always-running core. Dropping silence keeps storage, uploads and phone processing proportional to speech, and the journal turns 'it was recording' into 'it was saved'.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: An AVAudioEngine inputNode tap feeds a ~2 s ring buffer. A cheap RMS energy gate wakes SoundAnalysis (SNAudioStreamAnalyzer with the built-in classifier via SNClassifySoundRequest) to check for the speech class. Encode speech, plus ~2 s pre-roll and ~1.5 s hangover, through AVAudioConverter/AVAudioFile to AAC mono 16 kHz at 32 kbps, about 0.5 MB per 2-minute segment. Write a JSON sidecar per segment (session id, sequence, wall-clock start/end, SHA-256, markers, close reason), flush it on close, and recover orphaned segments at launch. Never stop or re-activate the engine during silence, because it cannot be restarted from the background; gating happens only at the encoder.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Delivery ledger with receipts and one-line status
minimal_watch_set.description: Segments move to the iPhone automatically and are deleted from the watch only after the phone confirms receipt. The complication shows one honest line: recording time, number queued, last sync.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Lost or never-transferred recordings are the top complaint (Omi's 11 h loss, Voice Memos truncation). Visible sync states are why people trust Granola's watch app.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Call WCSession.transferFile(_:metadata:) for each closed segment, with sequence number and hash in the metadata. The iPhone's session(_:didReceive:) verifies the hash and acks with transferUserInfo; sendMessage fails when the iPhone app is in the background. Delete a segment only after its ack, watch outstandingFileTransfers, and re-queue transfers that go stale. If the phone is unreachable, upload directly over Wi-Fi or cellular with a standard URLSession while the audio session gives the app runtime (DTS, forum 843751), and use a background URLSession only after the session ends. Test on a device, because transferFile doesn't work in the Simulator.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Interruption detection, one-tap resume, recorded gaps
minimal_watch_set.description: When a call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app takes the mic, the app closes the segment, logs a gap with its reason, taps the wrist once with 'Tap to resume', and shows Paused on the complication until the user resumes.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Capture can't be resumed from the background, so without this an 'always-running' app quietly stops at the first phone call; interruptions are the second most common complaint. Gap markers keep summaries honest about what wasn't heard.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Observe AVAudioSession interruption, route-change and media-services-reset notifications. On an interruption beginning, close the segment and write a GAP record. Post a local notification with interruptionLevel .timeSensitive and a foreground 'Resume' action, and reload the complication timeline to Paused. The app opens to a full-screen Resume button with .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction), which re-activates the session as a user-initiated foreground event. Send at most one follow-up reminder after about 10 minutes. Never try to restart in the background when the interruption ends.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Pause and Stop (bystander mode)
minimal_watch_set.description: Pause (15 min, 1 h, or until resumed) discards audio in memory and saves nothing. Stop turns the mic off. Both are one tap from the recording screen, and a timed Pause resumes without the user returning to the app.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Social acceptability is what kills always-on wearables: the Limitless user stopped wearing it socially, and Bee was banned at home. Users must be able to honour 'please don't record' instantly, and all-party consent law and the EDPB make it a compliance need.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Soft pause keeps AVAudioEngine and the session running (they can't be restarted from the background), drops frames before the encoder, writes PAUSE start/end markers, and shows 'Paused - not saving'. The orange mic indicator stays on, and the screen says so. A timed pause resumes writing in the background because the session never ended. Stop calls setActive(false), and restarting needs a foreground tap. On the paused screen, Resume is the primary action; a Control can open the app straight to this screen.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Battery and storage guardrails with projected hours
minimal_watch_set.description: The app measures this watch's actual drain during the session, shows 'about X h left at this rate', drops the bitrate in Low Power Mode, and stops cleanly at a battery floor (default 15%) or when storage runs low, with a final haptic.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: A dead watch fails at its main job and ends the habit. Battery uncertainty is a top-10 complaint and every public figure is a vendor claim. A clean auto-stop also prevents corrupt segments.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Turn on WatchKit battery monitoring and read the battery level at each segment close to compute %/h. Check free space before each segment and stop below 100 MB. Watch the Low Power Mode state and switch to 24 kbps when it is on. At a threshold, close the segment, call setActive(false), and send a haptic and a notification. Keep the recording screen static, with no timers or waveform animation, while the wrist is down. Whether recording keeps running under Low Power Mode is untested; check it on a device.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Moment bookmark (Double Tap: 'flag that')
minimal_watch_set.description: While recording, Double Tap or a tap on the main button flags the last ~60 seconds. The phone pins that span and its transcript to the top of the day and weights it in summaries and action items.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: It turns an ambient firehose into intent at almost no cost, needs no transcription on the watch, and covers the 'remember this' and 'what did they just say' jobs on watches without Live Rewind. It is a proven hardware affordance (Plaud NotePin S, Soundcore Work, Vocci, Flowtica).
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: On the recording screen the main button carries .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction). watchOS brings the app back on wrist raise during a background session, so flagging takes one raise and a pinch. Write {timestamp, lookback 60 s} into the open segment's sidecar and play a click haptic. The ring buffer and segments already written hold the audio, so nothing extra is recorded. Avoid the Crown double-press.

minimal_watch_set.feature: Glanceable payoff: today's coverage and top 1-3 items
minimal_watch_set.description: A Smart Stack widget or complication shows today's captured hours and gaps. Once the phone has processed the day, it adds the 1-3 commitments or decisions worth acting on. A tap shows a short read-only list; everything else stays on the phone.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Capture without a visible reward loses users. This closes the habit loop on the device where the habit lives, fills the 'capture-only, can't review on the wrist' gap, and answers 'did it work?' without opening the phone.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: The iPhone pushes a compact payload (coverage, gap count, up to 3 items with due dates and span IDs) through updateApplicationContext for latest-state data, or transferUserInfo. The watch saves it to an App Group store and reloads the WidgetKit timelines. RelevanceKit raises the 'Start my day' widget in the morning and the recap in the evening. The watch has no chat, no transcripts and no editing; 'Send to Reminders' runs on the phone.

explicitly_cut.feature: Transcription on the watch / live transcript on the wrist
explicitly_cut.reason: watchOS has no SFSpeechRecognizer or SpeechAnalyzer. System dictation returns final text only and stops silently after ~30-45 s. Streaming text back from the phone costs battery and needs networking the watch restricts. Transcripts belong on the phone.

explicitly_cut.feature: A Live Rewind clone on the Digital Crown
explicitly_cut.reason: On Series 12 and Ultra 4 the Crown double-press belongs to Apple's free Live Rewind. A rewind needs low-latency speech recognition the watch lacks. The Double Tap bookmark covers the 'flag what was just said' job.

explicitly_cut.feature: Hands-free start, wake word, scheduled auto-start, auto-resume after interruptions
explicitly_cut.reason: Not possible: capture must be started by the user in the foreground and cannot be resumed from the background (forum 750432). A one-tap resume nudge replaces it now, and phone-side context prompts can come later.

explicitly_cut.feature: Keep-alives using HKWorkoutSession or WKExtendedRuntimeSession
explicitly_cut.reason: Both break App Review rules: guideline 2.5.4 (2.5.1 per the Earshot notes) bars using background services outside their purpose, and developers have been rejected repeatedly. Extended runtime sessions are capped at 10 min to 1 h, and a workout session pollutes the Activity rings and drains power.

explicitly_cut.feature: Real-time streaming to the phone or cloud (WebSocket / Network framework)
explicitly_cut.reason: TN3135 restricts low-level networking on watchOS. A developer measured the network path being revoked every ~36-38 s during an audio session (FB24377808), and streaming costs battery. Minutes of latency is fine for the jobs this app serves.

explicitly_cut.feature: AI chat / Ask on the watch in v1
explicitly_cut.reason: The watch has no on-device LLM. PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel needs a managed entitlement and has daily quotas. Petey's 3.8 rating shows chat on the wrist is hard to get right. It comes after reliability is proven.

explicitly_cut.feature: Summaries, transcript browsing or action-item editing on the watch
explicitly_cut.reason: The screen is too small and editing costs battery. The phone owns review; the watch shows at most 1-3 read-only items.

explicitly_cut.feature: Proactive nudges beyond the resume prompt and the optional evening glance
explicitly_cut.reason: Friend's unprompted texts read as intrusive and Omi drew 'micromanager' criticism. Notification fatigue erodes the habit and uses battery. Nudges belong behind a gate on the phone.

explicitly_cut.feature: Identifying bystanders by name / voiceprints of others
explicitly_cut.reason: Bystander voiceprints may be GDPR Art. 9 biometric data, and voiceprints raise consent problems. The minimal system separates only the wearer from everyone else, on the phone.

explicitly_cut.feature: Integrations, templates and agent setup on the watch
explicitly_cut.reason: These are phone and web jobs. Keeping the watch binary small and single-purpose makes it more reliable.

explicitly_cut.feature: Keeping full raw audio forever by default
explicitly_cut.reason: It adds storage cost and legal exposure: all-party consent states, and the EDPB's recommendation that persistent storage be off by default. A short verification window with transcripts kept longer gives most of the trust benefit.

explicitly_cut.feature: Recording in Opus or LPCM
explicitly_cut.reason: Opus encoding on the watch is unverified, and LPCM is ~115 MB/h. AAC mono at 24-32 kbps is ~10.8-14.4 MB/h and works on the watch.

explicitly_cut.feature: Relying on AudioRecordingIntent / Live Activity for the recording indicator
explicitly_cut.reason: Its behaviour on watchOS is unclear: the docs require a Live Activity, but Activity.request lists only iOS and macOS. The system's orange mic indicator plus a clear in-app state are enough. Test it later.

explicitly_cut.feature: Wrist-flick or pinch triggers, health/location fusion, translation
explicitly_cut.reason: Wrist flick and the watchOS 27 single pinch have no developer API. Health and location context and translation are enrichments, not the core value.

explicitly_cut.feature: Live waveform or animated always-on display during capture
explicitly_cut.reason: It uses battery for no informational value while the wrist is down. A static Recording/Paused state communicates what matters.

proposals.architecture_notes:
JOBS, IN PRIORITY ORDER: (1) Never lose what was said in conversations that matter: in-person work talk, 1:1s, hallway decisions. (2) Surface the few commitments and decisions worth acting on. (3) Let the user find and check a detail later. Quick voice notes use the same session: bookmark, then speak. The watch is a thin, honest recorder; the iPhone does the thinking; the cloud is optional and needs consent.

CAPTURE (watch):
- The session is user-started in the foreground, from a complication, Control, Action Button or Double Tap. Activate AVAudioSession(.record) once per session and never re-activate it from the background. Re-activation fails in the background (forum 750432), and repeated activation is linked to the ~36-38 s network-path revocation (forum 841590).
- An AVAudioEngine input tap feeds a ~2 s ring buffer. An RMS energy gate wakes the SoundAnalysis built-in classifier's speech check, and only speech (with pre-roll and hangover) is encoded. The mic and engine keep running through silence and soft Pause; gating happens only at the encoder.
- Encoding is AAC mono 16 kHz at 32 kbps (24 kbps in Low Power Mode), in 2-minute segments with JSON sidecars: sequence, wall-clock times, SHA-256, bookmark, pause and gap markers, and close reason. Segments are journaled and recovered at launch.
- On an interruption: close the segment with its reason, write a GAP, send a time-sensitive notification with a haptic ('Tap to resume'), and switch the complication to Paused. Resuming needs a foreground tap.
- No workout or extended-runtime keep-alives.
- Target watchOS 27 (Series 9+, Ultra 2+, SE 3) with a watchOS 26 fallback. Leave the Crown double-press alone on Series 12 and Ultra 4.

SYNC:
- Primary path: WCSession.transferFile per segment, with hash metadata. The iPhone verifies the hash and acks with transferUserInfo, because sendMessage fails when the iPhone app is in the background. The watch deletes a segment only after its ack, and stale entries in outstandingFileTransfers are retried.
- When the phone is unreachable: upload directly over Wi-Fi or cellular to the user's CloudKit private database or an HTTPS endpoint. Use a standard URLSession while the audio session gives the app runtime, and a background URLSession only after the session ends.
- Source conflict: the Earshot notes say to always use background transfers (about 4 refreshes an hour with a complication on the face). The tech brief cites DTS (forum 843751) saying background uploads may wait for Wi-Fi and suggesting a standard session during runtime the app already has. I used the more specific DTS guidance for uploads during a session and the Earshot approach afterwards.
- Segment length: the brief says 1-5 min and Earshot says 2 min. I chose 2 min. At about 0.5 MB a segment is far below the reported sub-30 MB transferFile failure, and a lost segment costs little.
- Results flow back to the watch through updateApplicationContext or transferUserInfo into an App Group store that the complications and Smart Stack read. Expect minutes of latency. No WebSocket or live streaming (TN3135).

TRANSCRIPTION AND AI:
- Watch: voice-activity detection only. There is no Speech framework and no on-device LLM on the watch.
- iPhone (a required companion):
  - Transcription: SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber (iOS 26+) gives free, private, timestamped long-form transcripts. SpeechTranscriber has no custom vocabulary (per Argmax) and covers a limited set of languages; WhisperKit is the fallback for both, but check that it runs on iOS.
  - Speakers: start with wearer-versus-others from a short voice enrollment. Full diarization (pyannote community-1 via SpeakerKit/FluidAudio) is verified only on the Mac, so test it on iPhone or run it in the cloud tier.
  - Media filtering: SoundAnalysis classes, plus ShazamKit per the Earshot notes.
  - Free-tier summaries: Apple Foundation Models on the iPhone with @Generable schemas, sized to the 4,096-token session context. Summarise per conversation, then roll up into a daily summary.
- Paid cloud tier: runs only after explicit consent to third-party AI (guideline 5.1.2(i)), and everything passes through one redaction gate that logs every payload.
  - Models: claude-haiku-5-5 for per-conversation extraction, claude-opus-5-5 for nightly synthesis. Run nightly and weekly work on Message Batches at 50% cost.
  - Follow the API rules recorded in the Earshot notes: no temperature or top_p, control depth with effort, use structured outputs, and check for refusals.
  - Keys never ship in clients: use your own proxy or the beta ClaudeForFoundationModels package with .appAttest.
- Don't build core features on Private Cloud Compute (PCC): it needs a managed entitlement and has daily quotas.
- Every derived item carries source span IDs, and a capture-coverage table lets answers say 'not recorded'.
- Heavy processing runs while the phone charges overnight and right away when the app opens. The research doesn't verify iOS background limits for long transcription, so show processing status honestly.

DATA:
- The watch holds only segments the phone hasn't acknowledged.
- The phone vault holds transcripts (kept until the user deletes them), derived items with spans, and audio for a short verification window: 7 days by default, user-adjustable. 'Summary only' and 'wearer only' modes cover strict jurisdictions.
- Data is encrypted at rest. Multi-device sync uses the CloudKit private database, so the vendor holds no copy by default.
- The export schema is documented.

BATTERY BUDGET:
- Rated battery life: Series 11/12 24 h, SE 3 18 h, Ultra 3 42 h, Ultra 4 50 h.
- Research estimate (low confidence) for continuous recording down to a 10-15% floor: Series 11/12 about 10-14 h, SE 3 about 8-11 h, Ultra 3 about 18-24 h. Vendor claims range from 3%/h with the screen off to 15-20%/h.
- Target: total drain at or below ~6%/h while recording on Series 11/12, so a 07:00-19:00 workday ends at 20-25% or more. Ultra models should cover a 16 h waking day, and SE 3 gets a 'workday' profile.
- Where the power goes: the mic and AAC encoder run continuously. SoundAnalysis runs only when the energy gate trips. The radio wakes in short batches (transferFile is throttled by the OS anyway). No UI work wrist-down, no PCC calls, no streaming.
- Storage: about 10.8-14.4 MB per hour of speech. A fully ungated 16 h day is about 175-230 MB, and acked segments are deleted.
- Guards: stop at 15% battery or under 100 MB free, and lower the bitrate in Low Power Mode. Whether recording survives Low Power Mode is untested.
- Instrument drain per model from the first prototype, show projected hours, and publish no battery claims until they are measured.

OTHER CONFLICTS RESOLVED:
- App Review: the brief says Apple never answered whether long recording is accepted. The Earshot notes cite an actual rejection in which reviewers said the audio background mode is for playback (forum 776949). I weighted the specific rejection and treat it as the top risk.
- Granola: the Earshot notes and the brief say it keeps recording wrist-down, while heise says it must stay in the foreground and stops if you check a text or set a timer. My reading: wrist-down is fine, but switching to an app that takes the audio session ends capture. Apple's engineer confirms recording continues in the background, so test continuity while using other apps.
- Pebble Index 01 (catalog: $75 and in stock) and Sandbar Stream Ring (catalog: shipping since early November 2026): I used the catalog's more recent product-page checks over the Earshot notes.
risks: App Review could reject all-day recording under the audio background mode. A developer was rejected because reviewers said the mode is for playback (forum 776949), DTS cannot speak for App Review, and Apple did not answer in forum 750432. This is existential for the watch app. Mitigation: TestFlight first, Meet with Apple before submitting, user-started sessions only, obvious indicators, no keep-alive tricks.

Apple could sherlock the product. Siri Recap and Live Rewind (watchOS 27.3, expected December) are free and built in. If Apple extends them to older watches, more languages or the EU, or adds transcripts and speaker labels, the opening narrows to citations, export, integrations and retention. There is no API to build on Apple's Audio Intelligence, and mic contention between our session and Apple's on Series 12/Ultra 4 is untested.

Real battery drain has never been measured. Every number is a vendor claim or a low-confidence estimate (about 10-14 h of recording on Series 11/12, 8-11 h on SE 3). If drain lands near the reported 15-20%/h, 'always running' shrinks to 'meetings only' and the product thesis changes. Measure per model in week one.

The platform is fragile, and each weakness below can lose data silently unless the delivery ledger and coverage UI catch it:
- Calls, Siri, alarms and other audio apps end capture, and it can't restart until the user taps.
- transferFile is throttled by the OS, and one developer reports a file under 30 MB failing.
- The network path was revoked every ~36-38 s during an audio session (FB24377808).
- Behaviour under Low Power Mode, and of AudioRecordingIntent/Live Activity on the watch, is unverified.

Legal and consent exposure is growing (not legal advice; get counsel before an EU launch or workplace marketing):
- Wiretap/CIPA suits: Brewer v. Otter.ai and Subia v. Meta are verified; Chamberlain v. Granola is not.
- 11-13 US states require all-party consent.
- EDPB Statement 01/2026 says consent obtained after recording is invalid and recommends persistent storage off by default.
- Germany's §201 StGB carries criminal penalties.
- Workplace policies may forbid recording.
- Bystander voiceprints may count as GDPR Art. 9 biometric data.

Bad AI output could collapse trust. Hallucinations, TV treated as conversation and speaker confusion (Bee) erode it fast, and one wrong 'you promised X' on the wrist does lasting damage. The mitigations are citations, an audio window for checking, media filtering, and a self-check before anything reaches the watch.

Habits decay and people reject the device socially. The long-term Limitless user dropped it from social settings, then from casual meetings, until only calls remained, and judged about 10% of captures valuable. A Bee user's partner banned it at home. If the evening payoff isn't reliably useful, users stop tapping Start, and unwanted proactivity (Friend, Omi) speeds up churn.

iPhone background processing is unverified. WCSession delivers files in the background, but the research doesn't confirm that long SpeechAnalyzer jobs can run in iOS background tasks, or that diarization works on the iPhone (it is verified on the Mac). Transcripts may wait for charging or for the app to open, bringing back the 'summaries never arrive' complaint.

Wrist-mic audio quality is unknown. The research has no evidence on across-the-table pickup, clothing rustle or sleeve occlusion compared with dedicated multi-mic devices (Plaud Note Pro's 4 mics, Comu Action Pro's 6, Legend One's 3). Poor audio limits transcript quality whatever the models.

Cheap dedicated hardware undercuts the watch's convenience advantage. Bee Frontier costs $74.99 with a 7-day battery and integrates with Apple Watch, Pebble Index 01 costs $75 with no subscription, and Plaud leads the category with long battery and 64 GB of storage.

Cloud synthesis economics are a risk. All-day transcripts are large, and Opus at $4/$20 per MTok gets expensive if run per chunk. Bulk work goes to on-device Foundation Models (whose 4,096-token context limits quality) or to Haiku, nightly jobs run on batches at 50% off, and capture and transcription stay free so pricing isn't metered by the minute.

Soft pause is ambiguous. To allow a timed auto-resume the mic stays open, so the orange indicator stays on while the screen says 'Paused', and bystanders may not believe it. Offer a hard Stop and explain the difference plainly.

Users fear the vendor will disappear. Humane bricked its devices, and Limitless turned off capture and deleted regional data within two weeks of being acquired. Without open export and local-first storage, prospects will hesitate to trust the product with their memory.
Any watch-side AI that depends on PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel is exposed: the managed entitlement could be denied, and daily per-user quotas can cut features off in the middle of the day.

best_feature_set.feature: One-tap, user-started all-day capture session
best_feature_set.description: A single 'Start capture' tap from a complication, Smart Stack widget, watchOS 26 Control (opens the app), the Ultra Action Button, or Double Tap on the in-app Start button. The session starts in the foreground and then keeps running wrist-down in the background for hours with the screen off.
best_feature_set.rationale: This is the only legitimate long-recording path on watchOS [H]: an audio-mode session the user starts in the foreground. One-tap start is the most-loved watch capture feature, and every shipping watch recorder works this way. Voice-triggered, scheduled or automatic start is impossible for third parties.

best_feature_set.feature: Never-lose-a-minute pipeline: crash-safe chunks, receipt ledger, visible sync states
best_feature_set.description: Audio is written as short AAC segment files, each with a journal entry. A segment is deleted from the watch only after the iPhone confirms it has a durable copy. Every segment shows Recorded > Queued > On iPhone > Transcribed, with automatic retry.
best_feature_set.rationale: The number-one complaint is recordings lost or never transferred: Omi lost 11 h, Voice Memos truncated recordings, Drafts broke after a watchOS update. Losing data hurts trust more than any missing feature. Granola's explicit sync states are the reference design.

best_feature_set.feature: Interruption recovery with gap markers and a one-tap resume nudge
best_feature_set.description: When a call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app interrupts capture, the app closes the open segment and records a GAP with its reason. It then sends one time-sensitive haptic notification ('Tap to resume') and switches the complication to a Resume state. Gaps show in the timeline and are passed to the summarizer so the AI never makes up content for them.
best_feature_set.rationale: Capture stopping on interruption is the second most common complaint. Resuming from the background is impossible [H], so the best achievable experience is fast detection, an honest gap, and a one-tap foreground resume.
exemplars: Granola (interrupted recordings sync partially but cannot resume)
Apple Voice Memos & Notes audio transcription (complaint: alarms stop recordings)

best_feature_set.feature: Unmistakable recording state, consent reminder, true one-tap pause
best_feature_set.description: The system orange mic indicator, plus a start/stop haptic and chime and a distinctive full-screen recording state. A consent reminder appears at session start. Pause actually stops the mic, so the indicator goes off and nothing is buffered.
best_feature_set.rationale: Required by App Review 2.5.14 (consent plus a clear indication). The EDPB says consent obtained after recording is invalid and indicators should be on by default. Apple's Live Rewind chimes even on silent, which sets the bar. Users abandon these devices first in social settings, so an instant, real pause protects retention.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Full timestamped transcript with source-audio playback for verification
best_feature_set.description: A complete transcript per segment with timestamps. Tapping any line plays the original audio for a short default retention window, after which only the transcript is kept unless the user chooses otherwise.
best_feature_set.rationale: Apple's Siri Recap is summary-only, with no transcript. Bee deletes audio, so reviewers could not check its output when it treated TV as conversation. Being able to verify against the transcript and audio is the clearest gap a third party can fill.
exemplars: Bee Frontier (counter-example: no audio to verify)

best_feature_set.feature: Summaries and action items that cite transcript spans
best_feature_set.description: Per-session and per-day summaries and to-dos, built on the iPhone (on-device Foundation Models where available, or a cloud LLM after explicit consent). Every claim links to the transcript lines it came from.
best_feature_set.rationale: Summaries are expected (auto_summaries appears in 165 of 272 catalog products). Hallucinated or unverifiable summaries are a top complaint about Bee and Siri Recap, so citations make the output trustworthy.

best_feature_set.feature: Searchable day timeline and Ask over history, with honest coverage
best_feature_set.description: An iPhone timeline of captured and not-captured periods, full-text search, and natural-language Ask with cited answers. When asked about a period that wasn't recorded, it says so, using the coverage table instead of guessing.
best_feature_set.rationale: This is what users come back for ('what did we decide?'). Searchable memory and ask-over-history are among the most common features in the catalog (111 and 112 products).

best_feature_set.feature: Retention, privacy and AI-sharing controls
best_feature_set.description: Per mode, keep summary only, transcript, or transcript plus audio, with auto-delete windows. Storage is local-first and encrypted. A single consent gate covers any third-party AI call (guideline 5.1.2(i)), and delete-everything takes one tap.
best_feature_set.rationale: Apple has set the privacy baseline: opt-in, 7-day default retention, end-to-end encryption, sensitive-data filters. Litigation against Otter and Meta is rising, and the EDPB says persistent storage should be off by default. Users want a choice of what to keep, which is a listed unmet need.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Battery and storage guards with honest projected hours
best_feature_set.description: Capture stops cleanly at 15% battery or under 100 MB free, drops bitrate in Low Power Mode, and the complication shows a projected 'about X h left' based on measured drain.
best_feature_set.rationale: Battery is the least-measured part of the category; nearly every figure is a vendor claim. Draining the user's watch to zero is a reason to uninstall. Apple rates Series 12 at about 24 h for everything, so the budget has to be visible.

best_feature_set.feature: Open export and read-only agent access (API/MCP)
best_feature_set.description: Bulk export (Markdown, JSON, audio) and a read-only MCP server or API so Claude, ChatGPT and other agents can query transcripts, with redaction and an audit log.
best_feature_set.rationale: Agent access is now expected; Granola, Otter, Omi, Screenpipe, Monologue and Pebble all offer it. Bulk export and memory you can take elsewhere are listed unmet needs. Limitless's shutdown made data portability a selling point.

best_feature_set.feature: Reliable 'me vs others' speaker separation and wearer-only mode
best_feature_set.description: Diarization on the iPhone or Mac, with the wearer enrolled so 'me' is labeled reliably. An optional wearer-only retention mode drops other speakers' content.
best_feature_set.rationale: Diarization is weak nearly everywhere (Bee, Limitless, Granola), and Siri Recap does not attempt it. Wearer-only mode is the strongest answer to bystander and consent objections. Voiceprints are enrolled for the wearer only, because bystander voiceprints may be GDPR Art. 9 biometric data.

best_feature_set.feature: Bookmark or highlight a moment
best_feature_set.description: While recording, a Double Tap (or a tap on the recording screen) drops a timestamped highlight with a haptic confirmation. Highlights are weighted in summaries and jump straight to that moment in the timeline.
best_feature_set.rationale: Cheap to build, users love it on dedicated recorders, and it adds intent to ambient capture. It replaces the Live Rewind gesture, which belongs to Apple on Series 12 and Ultra 4.

best_feature_set.feature: Context-aware start prompts in place of automatic start
best_feature_set.description: A calendar event, a saved place, or a recurring time window triggers a haptic notification or Smart Stack card ('Team sync starting – Start capture?'). One tap starts capture in the foreground.
best_feature_set.rationale: Scheduled or ambient automatic start is impossible for third parties [H], while Siri Recap can be scheduled by time and place. A well-timed prompt gets close to Apple's behaviour without breaking platform rules, but nudges must be rare and under the user's control.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind) (scheduling by time/place)

best_feature_set.feature: Reach where Apple stops
best_feature_set.description: Supports Series 9 and later and SE 3 on watchOS 26/27, more languages, the EU (with stricter defaults), retention beyond 7 days, and full transcripts.
best_feature_set.rationale: Siri Recap is limited to Series 12/Ultra 4 with an iPhone 16 or later, English only, no EU, and no transcripts or speaker labels. Those limits are the market that is open to a third party.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind) (counter-example: hardware/region/language gated)

best_feature_set.feature: Glanceable results back on the wrist
best_feature_set.description: The iPhone pushes the latest summary, open to-dos and sync or coverage status to a complication and a Smart Stack widget (RelevanceKit), with no heavy browsing on the watch.
best_feature_set.rationale: Reviewing on the wrist is an unmet need; today watch apps only capture. Widgets are cheap and battery-friendly compared with an on-watch transcript browser.

best_feature_set.feature: Approval-gated routing of action items
best_feature_set.description: To-dos go to Reminders, Things or Todoist, and email or Slack drafts are prepared. Nothing executes without explicit approval on the iPhone. Every action is journaled.
best_feature_set.rationale: Hands-free routing is a top use case, and approval-gated agents are where leaders (Plaud Agent, Vocci) have converged. Keeping approval on the phone limits the blast radius.

best_feature_set.feature: Jurisdiction-aware consent tooling and pause zones
best_feature_set.description: Stricter defaults in all-party-consent states and the EEA/UK. Places and Focus modes can auto-prompt a pause (home, doctor, therapist), and an optional spoken or visible notice script is provided for others.
best_feature_set.rationale: There are 11–13 US all-party-consent states, the EDPB statement, and Germany's §201 StGB. Users abandon these devices first in social settings, and one Bee user's partner banned it at home.

best_feature_set.feature: Local-first vault, no-account mode, low or no subscription
best_feature_set.description: On-device transcription and summaries by default. An open, documented storage format. Cloud AI is optional or bring-your-own-key, with a one-time-purchase or generous free tier.
best_feature_set.rationale: Subscription fatigue (Bee $11.99, Omi $29.99, Plaud up to $239.99/yr) and shutdown risk (Humane bricked, Limitless deleted regional data) make local-first and no-subscription selling points. On-device processing also keeps marginal cost near zero.

best_feature_set.feature: Daily/weekly synthesis, people and project pages, commitment tracking
best_feature_set.description: Nightly and weekly rollups (batch-processed), per-person and per-project pages, and tracking of promises made, with at most a couple of nudges a day.
best_feature_set.rationale: High value but easy to get wrong: Friend's unprompted texts and Omi's 'micromanager' reputation show the backlash. It depends on a trustworthy Core transcript and citations first.

best_feature_set.feature: Ask from the wrist
best_feature_set.description: Ask a question by voice on the watch and get a short cited answer from your own history, relayed through the iPhone or answered through a cloud model.
best_feature_set.rationale: There is no on-device LLM or Speech framework on the watch. PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel needs a managed entitlement and has daily quotas, so it can't be a core dependency. The earshot notes report a beta ClaudeForFoundationModels package for watchOS 27, which I have not verified.
exemplars: Petey - AI Chat for Watch (formerly WatchGPT)

best_feature_set.feature: Mac/desktop botless meeting capture in the same timeline
best_feature_set.description: A Mac app captures call audio and merges it with watch sessions into one day.
best_feature_set.rationale: Covers online meetings, which the watch handles poorly, and gives power users a Mac workflow, which Apple lacks. It is a separate product surface with its own permissions and distribution decisions.

best_feature_set.feature: Health and location context on the timeline
best_feature_set.description: Visits (CLVisit), workouts and sleep or heart-rate context from HealthKit annotate the timeline and improve search ('the conversation at the clinic').
best_feature_set.rationale: A useful differentiator, but it adds permissions and privacy surface. It is not needed for the core value of not missing anything and finding it later.

best_feature_set.feature: Phone-call capture
best_feature_set.description: Import or capture both sides of phone calls with notifications to all parties.
best_feature_set.rationale: Legally complex, and Apple's Phone app already records calls with a notice to participants. Watch capture pauses during calls anyway.
exemplars: Apple Voice Memos & Notes audio transcription (Apple Intelligence)

minimal_watch_set.feature: 1. One-tap foreground start of a long-running capture session
minimal_watch_set.description: 'Start capture' from a complication, Smart Stack widget, Control, the Ultra Action Button, or Double Tap on the Start button. After the start, capture keeps running wrist-down with the screen off.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: This is the product. It is also the only legitimate way to record for hours on watchOS [H]. If starting isn't a single tap, people don't capture.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Declare the audio background mode in Info.plist. In the foreground, call AVAudioSession.sharedInstance().setCategory(.record) then setActive(true) once, and start AVAudioEngine with an inputNode.installTap. Never re-activate the session in a loop, because of the ~36–38 s network-revocation bug, FB24377808. Entry points: WidgetKit accessory complications and a Smart Stack widget that deep-link into the app; a watchOS 26 ControlWidget that opens the app (Controls run in the widget extension, so they must hand off to the foreground app); the Ultra Action Button through that Control or a Shortcut; and .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) on the Start button for Double Tap (S9+ and SE 3; not in Low Power Mode or with the wrist down). Do not use HKWorkoutSession or WKExtendedRuntimeSession as a keep-alive. Leave the Crown double-press alone, since it is Live Rewind on Series 12 and Ultra 4. Test AudioRecordingIntent on a device: its docs mention a Live Activity requirement on watchOS that is unclear [L].

minimal_watch_set.feature: 2. Crash-safe segmented recording on the watch
minimal_watch_set.description: Speech is encoded as AAC mono at 16 kHz and 24–32 kbps into 2-minute .m4a segment files. Each segment has a JSON sidecar and an entry in an append-only journal. On next launch the app recovers or finalizes any segment left open.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: A crash, low battery or a kill loses at most the current 2 minutes, never the day (compare Omi's 11-hour loss). Small segments also suit WCSession's undocumented size limits.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Feed tap buffers through AVAudioConverter into AVAudioFile(forWriting:settings:) with kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC. Opus on the watch is unverified, so use AAC only. Rotate files every 120 s (about 0.36–0.48 MB each). The sidecar holds seq, wall-clock start and end, sha256, bitrate and gap reason, and the journal is fsync'd after each rotation. At launch, scan the journal for an unclosed segment, finalize it if it is readable, and record a GAP if it is not.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 3. Receipt-based sync to the iPhone with a visible queue
minimal_watch_set.description: Each closed segment goes to the iPhone, which writes it durably and sends back an acknowledgement. Only then is the segment deleted from the watch. The watch shows a count of segments recorded, queued, on iPhone and transcribed.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: The top complaint in this category is recordings that never transfer. Receipts and visible states turn silent loss into a status the user can see and retry.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Call WCSession.default.transferFile(url, metadata:) per segment, then monitor outstandingFileTransfers and session(_:didFinish:error:) and retry on failure. The iPhone checks the hash and replies with transferUserInfo(['ack': seq]); avoid sendMessage, which fails when the iPhone app is in the background. If the iPhone has been unreachable for N minutes, upload to your own HTTPS or CloudKit endpoint with a standard URLSession during the runtime the recording session already provides (DTS guidance, forum 843751). Use a background URLSession only for leftovers after the session ends. Test on hardware with the iPhone's Bluetooth and Wi-Fi off, because the Simulator doesn't support transferFile.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 4. Interruption detection and one-tap resume
minimal_watch_set.description: A call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app ends capture. The app closes the segment and records a GAP with the reason. It then gives a haptic 'Recording paused by call – Tap to resume' and switches the complication to a Resume state.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Interruptions are unavoidable and can't be resumed from the background [H]. Without detection the user thinks they recorded the whole day, which is the worst failure possible.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Observe AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification, AVAudioSession.routeChangeNotification and AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange. On .began, finalize the segment, write a GAP sidecar, and schedule a UNNotificationRequest with interruptionLevel .timeSensitive (needs the Time Sensitive capability and user permission) and a 'Resume' UNNotificationAction with the .foreground option. Call WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines() to show the Resume state. Restart setActive(true) and engine.start() only on a user tap in the foreground; activating from the background fails ('Session activation failed').

minimal_watch_set.feature: 5. Clear recording state, consent reminder and true pause
minimal_watch_set.description: A full-screen recording state with color and elapsed time, start and stop haptics with an optional chime, and a consent reminder at session start. Pause turns the mic off; Resume takes one tap.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: App Review 2.5.14 requires explicit consent and a clear indication of recording. The EDPB says consent obtained after recording is invalid. A real pause is what keeps the watch on the wrist in social settings.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: The orange mic indicator is automatic and can't be hidden. Use WKInterfaceDevice.current().play(.start) and .play(.stop) for haptics. For Pause, call inputNode.removeTap and engine.stop() so the indicator clears and nothing is buffered. A user-paused session may suspend wrist-down, which is acceptable because Resume is a foreground tap (also bound to .handGestureShortcut). This user-driven stop and restart differs from automatic power gating, which must never stop the engine. Show the consent sheet on first run and a one-line reminder on each Start.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 6. Battery and storage guards with projected hours
minimal_watch_set.description: Capture stops cleanly at 15% battery or under 100 MB free. Bitrate drops in Low Power Mode. The complication shows a projected time remaining based on this session's measured drain.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Draining the user's watch to zero is grounds for uninstall. Real drain is unmeasured (vendor claims run from about 3%/h to 15–20%/h), so the app has to measure and be honest about it.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Set WKInterfaceDevice.current().isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true and read batteryLevel and batteryState at each segment rotation; log percent per hour to telemetry. Check free space with FileManager volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage and purge acknowledged segments first. Use ProcessInfo.processInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled and NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange to switch to 24 kbps. Whether recording works under Low Power Mode is untested [L], so verify. On a guard stop, finalize the segment, send one notification, and refresh the complication.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 7. iPhone companion that makes the audio useful: timestamped transcript, searchable timeline, tap-to-play
minimal_watch_set.description: Every synced segment is transcribed on the iPhone into a day timeline that shows gaps. Results are searchable, and tapping a line plays the source audio. The watch shows only a status line such as 'Transcribed through 10:42'.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: There is no speech recognition on the watch [H]. Without transcription and search this is just another Voice Memos. A full transcript with audio to check against is exactly what Siri Recap and Bee do not offer.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: On iOS 26+, run SpeechAnalyzer with SpeechTranscriber on each received segment and store timestamped results (audioTimeRange) in a local full-text-search database. Mark a segment transcribed and send transferUserInfo(['state': 'transcribed', 'seq': n]) to the watch, which updates its queue view and complication timeline. Nothing on the watch beyond receiving status.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 8. On-watch speech gating at the encoder (VAD)
minimal_watch_set.description: Silence and non-speech are dropped in RAM before encoding, with about 2 s of pre-roll and a 3–5 s hangover so word onsets and endings aren't clipped. A 'record everything' toggle is available.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: It cuts stored and transferred bytes, and with them radio energy and phone transcription time, by an unmeasured but likely large share of a mostly quiet day. It also means silence and background noise never reach disk. It ranks last because the pipeline works without it.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Compute per-buffer RMS with Accelerate (vDSP_rmsqv) against an adaptive noise floor, and keep a roughly 2 s ring buffer. Only when energy crosses the threshold, pass buffers to SNAudioStreamAnalyzer with SNClassifySoundRequest(classifierIdentifier: .version1) (SoundAnalysis, watchOS 9+) and check the 'speech' confidence. Write to the encoder only while speech plus hangover is active. The engine and mic keep running; gating happens only at the encoder. Measure CPU and battery with the gate on and off before shipping it on by default.

explicitly_cut.feature: Voice-triggered, scheduled or automatic start, and automatic resume after interruptions
explicitly_cut.reason: Not possible: capture must be started by the user in the foreground and can't be resumed from the background [H]. Use a one-tap start, context-aware start prompts (later) and resume nudges instead.

explicitly_cut.feature: HKWorkoutSession or WKExtendedRuntimeSession as a keep-alive
explicitly_cut.reason: Workout sessions for non-fitness use have led to repeated rejections (guidelines 2.5.4 and 2.5.1), drain battery, and move Activity rings. Extended runtime sessions are capped at 10 min to 1 h, allow one type per app, and are cancelled for sustained CPU.

explicitly_cut.feature: On-watch transcription, live captions or a live transcript on the wrist
explicitly_cut.reason: Neither SFSpeechRecognizer nor SpeechAnalyzer exists on watchOS [H]. System dictation stops after about 30–45 s and returns only final text. Streaming audio to the phone for live captions would need low-level networking, which TN3135 restricts and which suffers the 36–38 s revocation bug.

explicitly_cut.feature: On-watch LLM summaries or PCC-powered Ask in v1
explicitly_cut.reason: There is no on-device model on the watch [H]. PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel needs a managed entitlement, works online only and hits daily quotas (quotaLimitReached), so it is too fragile for a core feature. Summaries run on the iPhone.

explicitly_cut.feature: A Live Rewind clone (Crown double-press, 'what did they just say')
explicitly_cut.reason: On Series 12 and Ultra 4 the gesture belongs to Apple. Without ASR on the watch, round-trip latency to the phone would make it feel broken. Apple already ships it, so a highlight bookmark is the cheaper alternative.

explicitly_cut.feature: Real-time WebSocket or socket streaming to a cloud or Mac
explicitly_cut.reason: TN3135 allows low-level networking only for active audio streaming, CallKit VoIP or tvOS discovery. A watch app can't reach a Mac over Bonjour or raw TCP, and the path has been measured dropping every ~36–38 s. Chunked transferFile and URLSession are the reliable route.

explicitly_cut.feature: Wrist flick or single-pinch triggers
explicitly_cut.reason: No developer API exists [H].

explicitly_cut.feature: Hidden, discreet or indicator-suppressed recording
explicitly_cut.reason: The orange mic indicator can't be hidden [H]. Guidelines 2.5.14 and 2.5.19 forbid hiding recording, and it would invite wiretap and CIPA exposure (Brewer v. Otter, Subia v. Meta).

explicitly_cut.feature: Rich transcript browsing, search or editing on the watch
explicitly_cut.reason: A small screen, transfer cost and battery make it a poor fit. Glanceable widgets come later; real review happens on the iPhone.

explicitly_cut.feature: Proactive coaching or reminder notifications from the watch app
explicitly_cut.reason: Friend's unprompted texts and Omi's 'micromanager' reputation show the backlash, and it costs battery. The only notifications in v1 are resume, guard stops and sync errors.

explicitly_cut.feature: Bystander voiceprint enrollment or face/person identification
explicitly_cut.reason: Bystander voiceprints may be GDPR Art. 9 biometric data and raise consent risk in all-party states. Only the wearer gets enrolled, and that comes later, on the phone.

explicitly_cut.feature: Agentic actions executed from the watch (send email, post to Slack)
explicitly_cut.reason: A tiny approval surface and a large blast radius. Action routing comes later, gated by approval on the iPhone.

explicitly_cut.feature: Opus or other custom codecs
explicitly_cut.reason: Opus encoding on the watch is unverified; older reports say only AAC and LPCM work. Record AAC and transcode on the iPhone if needed.

explicitly_cut.feature: Live translation
explicitly_cut.reason: No speech recognition on the watch, latency-bound, and outside the core memory value. AirPods Pro 3 and Siri already cover it.

explicitly_cut.feature: Dependence on Apple's Siri Recap or Audio Intelligence
explicitly_cut.reason: No third-party API was found. It requires S11 Secure Exclave hardware, and the app should compete where Apple stops rather than build on it.

explicitly_cut.feature: Cloud LLM summaries enabled by default
explicitly_cut.reason: Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires disclosure and explicit permission before sharing with third-party AI. Default to on-device processing on the iPhone and make the cloud opt-in.

proposals.architecture_notes:
CAPTURE STRATEGY
- The watch is a thin, honest recorder. It runs one user-started foreground AVAudioSession (.record) in the audio background mode, with an AVAudioEngine input tap that keeps running wrist-down.
- The engine is never stopped automatically for power. Gating happens only at the encoder: an energy detector, confirmed by SoundAnalysis's speech class, with roughly 2 s of pre-roll and a 3–5 s hangover.
- An explicit user Pause really stops the engine. That is allowed because Resume is a foreground tap.
- Output is AAC mono, 16 kHz, 24–32 kbps, in 2-minute segments with JSON sidecars and an fsync'd journal.
- Interruptions (AVAudioSession interruption and route-change notifications, engine configuration changes) close the segment, write a GAP record with the reason, fire one time-sensitive 'Tap to resume' notification, and switch the complication to a Resume state.
- No HKWorkoutSession, no WKExtendedRuntimeSession, no Crown double-press.
- Target watchOS 27 on Series 9 and later, Ultra 2 and later, and SE 3, with a watchOS 26 fallback. Double Tap needs S9 or later and doesn't work in Low Power Mode or wrist-down.

WHERE TRANSCRIPTION AND AI RUN
- Nothing on the watch: it has no Speech framework and no on-device LLM.
- iPhone (required companion): SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber on iOS 26+ for timestamped long-form transcripts. It has no custom vocabulary and a limited set of languages at a time, so add WhisperKit later for gaps.
- Diarization (FluidAudio or SpeakerKit with pyannote community-1) is a Differentiator. Check iOS support; the earshot notes list SpeakerKit as macOS 14+ and put FluidAudio in its own module because it isn't Swift 6.
- Summaries and extraction use on-device Foundation Models on Apple Intelligence iPhones (4,096-token context per session, so chunk per segment and roll up), with every output carrying source span IDs.
- Optional cloud path, only after explicit consent under 5.1.2(i), through one logged egress gate:
  - claude-haiku-5-5 for bulk extraction ($0.10/$0.50 per MTok for prompts up to 100K).
  - claude-opus-5-5 for daily synthesis ($4/$20 per MTok, effort set explicitly, server-side fallback enabled).
  - Message Batches at a 50% discount for nightly and weekly rollups.
  - I checked these prices against the Claude API reference.
- PCC is never a core dependency (managed entitlement, daily quotas).
- A Mac is optional later for heavy re-transcription and diarization.

SYNC
- Primary path: WCSession.transferFile per segment, with seq and sha256 metadata. The iPhone writes the segment durably, then replies with transferUserInfo (not sendMessage). The watch deletes only after that receipt.
- States are visible on the watch and phone: Recorded > Queued > On iPhone > Transcribed.
- If the iPhone is unreachable for N minutes, upload with a standard URLSession during the recording session's runtime to your own HTTPS or CloudKit endpoint, batched about every 10 minutes on cellular. A background URLSession handles leftovers after the session ends.
- Expect minutes of latency, not real time.
- Keep a hashed ledger on both ends and an open, documented vault format: SQLite or JSON plus a Markdown mirror plus AAC.

BATTERY BUDGET
- No rigorous public measurement exists.
- Rated life: Series 11/12 24 h, SE 3 18 h, Ultra 3 42 h, Ultra 4 50 h, an average of about 4%/h for mixed use on Series 12.
- The brief's own estimate of 10–14 h from 100% to a 10–15% stop on Series 11/12 implies about 6–8.5%/h while recording [L]. SE 3 is about 8–11 h, Ultra 3 about 18–24 h.
- Vendor claims are not evidence: Hedy about 3%/h, others 15–20%/h, Granola 'more than a dozen hour-long meetings'.
- So the plan is:
  1. Screen off, no on-watch ML beyond the gated SoundAnalysis check.
  2. Prefer Bluetooth (WCSession) over Wi-Fi or cellular.
  3. Use the VAD to cut bytes.
  4. Stop at 15%, and step down to 24 kbps in Low Power Mode, whose recording behaviour is untested.
  5. Log percent per hour per model in telemetry and publish the real numbers.
- Market 'a workday of capture' on Series and SE models and a full day on Ultra, not 24/7.
- Data volume: ungated, 16 h is about 175–230 MB/day. Gated, my unverified assumption of 25–50% speech gives about 45–115 MB/day. Storage is not the constraint (about 64 GB).

SOURCE CONFLICTS AND WHICH I CHOSE
- (1) Segment length: the brief says 1–5 min and earshot says 2 min. I chose 2 min, which falls inside both ranges and keeps a crash loss small.
- (2) Upload path: earshot says 'always use background transfers' (about 4 refreshes an hour with a complication). The brief cites DTS (forum 843751) saying background URLSession may wait for Wi-Fi and to upload with a standard session during existing runtime. I chose the more specific DTS guidance while recording and background transfers only after the session ends.
- (3) Granola: the market scan says recording stops if you check a text or set a timer; earshot says it keeps recording wrist-down. I follow the Apple engineer's statement that recording continues in the background. Using other watch apps that touch audio, timers or Siri should be treated as interruptions until tested on a device.
- (4) The HKWorkoutSession guideline is cited as 2.5.4 (brief) and 2.5.1 (earshot). The outcome is the same: don't use it.
- (5) TN3135's 'active audio streaming' exception isn't a viable data path, given the earshot reading and the revocation bug, so there are no sockets or WebSockets.
- (6) For product status and price I prefer the catalog, dated Nov 16 (for example Stream Ring shipping and Pebble Index at $75), over the Nov 14 notes. Catalog records marked unchecked were sourced once.

BUILD EFFORT (my estimate, [L])
- The minimal watch app plus iPhone companion (items 1–8) is about one watchOS and one iOS engineer for 8–12 weeks to TestFlight.
- About half of that is an on-device reliability harness, because the Simulator lacks transferFile and allows low-level networking: forced interruptions, kill and crash recovery, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi off, Low Power Mode, and a 12 h soak per watch model.
- Hold a 'Meet with Apple' App Review consultation before public submission.
risks: App Review: recording in the audio background mode is not formally sanctioned. Apple documents it in playback terms; one developer reports a rejection because reviewers said audio mode is for playback (forum 776949); Apple did not answer the 'long user-started recording' question; DTS can't speak for App Review. Mitigate with TestFlight first, a Meet with Apple consultation, obvious indicators and consent, and positioning as user-started sessions rather than 24/7.

Apple is a direct competitor. Siri Recap and Live Rewind ship with watchOS 27.3 (expected in December) and make the 'ambient summary' pitch free. The defensible space is full transcripts, verification audio, speaker labels, retention beyond 7 days, older watches, non-English, the EU and agent access. Apple could expand into any of these.

Unrecoverable interruptions: calls, Siri, alarms, other audio apps and possibly timers end capture, and resuming needs a foreground tap. Heavy phone users will have many gaps and may tire of resume nudges, so coverage could be far below 'all day'.

Battery is unmeasured. My estimate is about 10–14 h on Series 11/12 and 8–11 h on SE 3 [L], so a full waking day may be impossible without a top-up. Low Power Mode recording behaviour and SoundAnalysis CPU cost are untested. Sustained CPU could get the app throttled or killed.

Sync fragility: transferFile is throttled for power, has no published size limit, fails in the Simulator, and one report describes a failure under 30 MB. Background URLSession may defer uploads until Wi-Fi. Any silent loss repeats Omi's 11-hour failure, so test with a ledger and soak tests on real devices.

A networking-path bug: the network path was revoked every ~36–38 s while an audio session was active, which DTS tied to repeated session activation (FB24377808). Any design that re-activates the session or depends on low-level networking risks breaking uploads.

Legal: 11–13 US all-party-consent states; the EDPB statement (Oct 13, 2026) says consent after recording is invalid and storage should be off by default; Germany's §201 StGB carries criminal penalties; wiretap and CIPA suits are active (Brewer v. Otter, Subia v. Meta), and early-2026 pleading-stage rulings largely favoured plaintiffs. The Granola suit is unverified. California's SB 1130 indicator mandate was vetoed but could return. Recording at work needs employer policy.

Privacy and social acceptance: users abandon always-on capture first in social settings (the long-term Limitless user, the Bee partner ban, the therapist objection). The EFF and press call Siri Recap 'creepy' or 'surveillance'. Without a wearer-only mode and pause zones, retention will suffer.

AI disclosure and biometrics: any cloud LLM call needs 5.1.2(i) disclosure and explicit permission. Bystander voiceprints may be GDPR Art. 9 biometric data, so diarization must avoid enrolling non-wearers.

Transcript quality on wrist audio is unproven: distant speakers, a sleeve over the mic, and TV or music treated as conversation (Bee). SpeechTranscriber lacks custom vocabulary and covers a limited set of languages at a time; its WER of 14.0 on earnings22 is a Mac benchmark, not wrist audio.

On-device AI limits: Foundation Models on the iPhone needs an Apple Intelligence iPhone and has a 4,096-token context, so summaries need chunking and rollups. Older iPhones fall back to cloud processing, which needs consent and costs money. Watch-side PCC has quotas and a managed entitlement.

AudioRecordingIntent's watchOS documentation says a Live Activity must run while recording, but Activity.request lists only iOS and macOS. If App Review or the system starts enforcing that, the capture flow may need rework [L].
