Economics: competitors offer free unlimited transcription (Pocket, Comulytic, HiDock) and one-time purchases (Just Press Record, Whisper Notes). Cloud transcription and LLM costs per hour of audio would squeeze a subscription, so on-device processing is a cost necessity, not just a privacy feature.

Evidence quality: battery figures, several product prices and statuses, and the Granola lawsuit are vendor claims or single-source. Catalog records marked unchecked were not re-verified. Treat roadmap decisions that hinge on them as provisional until tested on devices.

best_feature_set.feature: Intentional capture: Memo and Session modes (user-started only)
best_feature_set.description: Two capture modes, both started by the wearer. Memo is tap or hold to capture your own thought, kept as the wearer's speech. Session is one tap to start a long background capture (meeting, lecture, a block of the workday) that can be time-boxed ('until 6 pm'). A schedule only sends the user a reminder to tap; it never starts recording by itself. Capture is never voice-triggered or hidden. Marketing and UI copy say 'Session', never 'always listening'.
best_feature_set.rationale: watchOS only lets recording start from a foreground user action and cannot resume it from the background, so user initiation is a hard limit as well as the strongest legal and App Review position. The category is splitting into always-on products (Bee, Omi, Nirva, Siri Recap) and intentional ones (Pebble, Plaud, Sandbar, Live Rewind). A watch can credibly do intentional long Sessions. One-tap start is the watch feature users praise most.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Clear recording indicators and consent at the moment of capture
best_feature_set.description: The system orange mic indicator (it cannot be hidden), a start chime and haptic that are on by default and cannot be turned off in Session mode, a clear recording screen and a REC state on the complication. Onboarding asks where the user lives and sets defaults to match: the 13 all-party-consent US states on Kilpatrick's list, the EEA/UK, and Germany are strictest. Each Session in a strict jurisdiction shows a consent reminder, offers a one-tap 'Announce' that plays a short spoken notice, and records a consent entry with the session (announced or not, and how).
best_feature_set.rationale: App Store Guideline 2.5.14 requires a clear indication and explicit consent. The EDPB says indicators should be on by default and hard to turn off, and that consent obtained after recording is invalid. Limitless's own help center says an LED alone is 'not enough'. Only 76 of the 272 catalog products have consent controls, so this protects us legally and also sets us apart.
exemplars: Truecaller AI Call Recording (beep to other party)
Flowtica Verso (indicator cannot be disabled; launches Nov 17)
Google Intelligent Eyewear (recording stops if LED covered)
Google Meet 'Take notes for me' (Gemini) (admin-enforced consent)

best_feature_set.feature: Pause, Stop, schedules and pause zones
best_feature_set.description: An instant Pause (bystander mode) discards audio in memory, so nothing is analysed or saved. A full Stop releases the microphone. Capture pauses automatically during phone calls and FaceTime. Users can set quiet hours and link to Focus modes, and later tag places as pause zones (home, clinic, therapist, a child's school). A paused stretch leaves only a GAP marker.
best_feature_set.rationale: Social settings are the first thing users give up. A long-term Limitless user stopped wearing it socially, one Bee user's partner banned it at home, and a therapist objected. Limitless's guidance is to turn the device off when someone declines. Fellow removes paused segments entirely, and Siri Recap pauses during calls and can be scheduled. Making it easy to stop recording is what keeps people using it.
exemplars: Slack AI huddle notes (anyone can pause)
Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Minimise what is kept, starting with the wearer; retention the user chooses
best_feature_set.description: Silence is never written to disk. By default the wearer's own speech is kept as a transcript. Other people's speech is kept verbatim only where consent was logged or the jurisdiction allows; otherwise it is reduced to a summary with no quotes. Raw audio is kept encrypted for a short verification window (recommended default 72 h) and then crypto-shredded. Each Session can be set to summary only, transcript, or transcript plus audio. IDs, payment details, login data, health and self-harm content are filtered out before storage and before anything leaves the device.
best_feature_set.rationale: The EDPB recommends keeping persistent storage off by default and limiting continuous recording. Bee and Siri Recap discard audio, which leaves nothing to check summaries against. A short window balances trust against minimisation. Users have asked for retention they can choose, and Jump already sells it. Keeping less third-party speech reduces both legal exposure and breach exposure.
exemplars: Taya Necklace (voice fingerprint suppresses others; unshipped)
Bee Frontier (raw audio deleted, device-held keys)
Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind) (7-day deletion, sensitive filters)

best_feature_set.feature: Capture pipeline that never loses audio, with visible sync states
best_feature_set.description: Audio is saved in 2-minute segments recorded in a hashed ledger. A segment is deleted from the watch only after the iPhone confirms it has it. The app recovers after a crash, sends a resume prompt after an interruption, and writes GAP markers. A coverage timeline lets the assistant answer 'not recorded' instead of guessing. Sync states are visible: Recorded, Queued, On iPhone, Transcribed.
best_feature_set.rationale: The top complaint is recordings that are lost or never transfer: Omi lost 11 hours, Voice Memos truncated a recording, Drafts sync broke after a watchOS update. One such incident ends the trust a privacy-first brand depends on. Granola's visible states with retry are the model to follow.
exemplars: HiDock P1 (stays on device until upload)

best_feature_set.feature: Transcription on the user's own devices first, separation of 'me' from 'others', summaries that cite the transcript
best_feature_set.description: The iPhone transcribes with SpeechTranscriber; a Mac can optionally take over heavier diarization. Speech is separated into 'me' and 'others' using only the wearer's own enrolled voice. TV and music are filtered out. Summaries, decisions and action items link each sentence back to the transcript span it came from. Others are not named automatically.
best_feature_set.rationale: Accuracy failures hurt trust more than missing features do: Bee treated TV as conversation and its summaries hallucinated. Speaker diarization is weak across the category, and Apple does not attempt it. Processing on the user's devices keeps third-party speech off vendor servers and keeps per-user cost low.
exemplars: AWS HealthScribe (each sentence linked to transcript)
Rev (AI Notetaker and Voice Recorder app) (cited answers)

best_feature_set.feature: Local-first vault owned by the user, open export, no-account mode, exit guarantee
best_feature_set.description: Data is stored encrypted on the user's own devices, and the vendor holds no copy by default. Optional sync is end-to-end encrypted. Users can bulk-export to Markdown, JSON and AAC. The schema is documented and an open-source reader is published. One tap deletes everything, and any time range or session can be deleted, which also lets the user honour a bystander's deletion request.
best_feature_set.rationale: Within two weeks of its acquisition Limitless turned off capture and deleted regional data, and Humane devices were bricked. Users already complain about missing bulk export. Owning their data is the trust advantage incumbents cannot copy (Amazon, Meta, OpenAI). Only 59 of 272 catalog products are local-only or end-to-end encrypted.

best_feature_set.feature: Explicit consent for third-party AI, through a single exit point
best_feature_set.description: Cloud LLMs stay off until the user opts in to each provider. Names and numbers are redacted or pseudonymised on the device before anything is sent. All outbound calls go through one exit point that logs every payload. Providers must offer zero retention and no training. Users can bring their own API key.
best_feature_set.rationale: Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires disclosing sharing with third-party AI and getting explicit permission. The Brewer v. Otter.ai suit alleges the company trained on recordings. Grain advertises that it never trains on customer data. Any silent cloud call risks both rejection and a lawsuit.
exemplars: Claude voice mode (audio deleted after transcription)

best_feature_set.feature: Read-only agent access (MCP) with scopes and an audit log
best_feature_set.description: A local MCP server (stdio and localhost). It starts read-only, applies redaction, gives each client its own token and logs every request. Broad queries such as 'all of last week' need approval on the watch.
best_feature_set.rationale: Agent access is now expected: Granola, Otter, Omi, Pebble and Screenpipe all offer it. It is also a channel through which bystander speech can leak, so scopes and audit logs are where we can do better than others.

best_feature_set.feature: Fill the gaps Siri Recap leaves
best_feature_set.description: Full transcripts with me/others labels, retention beyond 7 days, support for Series 9+/SE 3 on watchOS 27 (with a watchOS 26 fallback) and for iPhones without Apple Intelligence, more languages, export and MCP. Recording continues while the user opens other watch apps. We match Apple's privacy features: opt-in, chime, schedules, sensitive-data filters.
best_feature_set.rationale: Siri Recap is free but needs a Series 12 or Ultra 4 plus an iPhone 16 or later. It is English-only, not available in the EU, produces summaries only with no speakers, and deletes them after 7 days. Granola's watch app stops if the user checks a text; background audio mode lets ours keep going.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)
Apple Watch native voice (watchOS 27 Siri AI, Siri Recap, Voice Memos, dictation)

best_feature_set.feature: Consent Kit and rights for bystanders
best_feature_set.description: A consent card the other person can open from a QR code or link on the iPhone, showing what is kept and offering a deletion request. A spoken announcement. Templates for notifying a workplace. A consent log that can be exported for each session. The other person's speech can be removed by time range or selection, with no voiceprint needed.
best_feature_set.rationale: The EDPB says manufacturers cannot push GDPR duties onto users. A watch looks like a watch, so bystanders cannot see that it is recording the way they can with a pendant LED, and the burden to disclose is higher. No catalog product offers deletion facing the bystander. Being comfortable using it socially is what keeps people using it.
exemplars: Axon Draft One (disclosure footers, audit logs)

best_feature_set.feature: Verification window and honest coverage
best_feature_set.description: Within the audio window, every claim in a summary links to the transcript and to playable audio. A coverage timeline shows the gaps. The assistant answers 'not recorded' instead of guessing, and uncertain speaker attribution is labelled as uncertain.
best_feature_set.rationale: Bee and Recap leave nothing to check. Summaries that put the wrong words in someone's mouth harm relationships and could be misused as evidence.
exemplars: Rev (AI Notetaker and Voice Recorder app)
Bee Frontier (no audio to verify, cautionary)

best_feature_set.feature: Pause by context, with defaults for sensitive places
best_feature_set.description: The iPhone pauses capture automatically in tagged places, during calendar events marked private or medical, during Focus modes and during calls. A filter for sensitive categories runs before storage. Session mode is 18+.
best_feature_set.rationale: The EDPB recommends geofencing. Medical, therapy, legal and school settings, and children as bystanders, carry the highest legal and reputational risk. Apple applies an 18+ limit to Recap.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Review and ask on the wrist
best_feature_set.description: A Smart Stack recap card and the day's action items. The user can ask about their memory from the watch, with the answer worked out on the iPhone and shown on the wrist.
best_feature_set.rationale: Users have asked for this: today watch apps only capture. Showing results on the wrist makes the capture feel worth doing.
exemplars: Pebble Time 2 / Pebble Round 2 (answers on watch)

best_feature_set.feature: Actions only with approval, with a journal and undo
best_feature_set.description: The assistant drafts reminders, calendar events and follow-up emails and never sends them on its own. Every executed action is journaled with its inverse so it can be undone. Double Tap may only trigger actions that cannot do damage.
best_feature_set.rationale: An agent working on other people's words has a large blast radius. Approval before acting is the norm among trusted products.
exemplars: Plaud Note Pro (Plaud Agent after approval)

best_feature_set.feature: Rare proactivity that the user controls
best_feature_set.description: A nudge must name the decision it helps with. The default is at most two a day, with quiet hours and batching. Notifications are passive by default and time-sensitive only for deadlines.
best_feature_set.rationale: Friend's unprompted texts felt intrusive, Omi was called a 'micromanager' and removed its automatic reflections. Unwanted nudges make users feel watched.

best_feature_set.feature: Local tier with no subscription
best_feature_set.description: Transcription and summaries on the user's own iPhone or Mac, sold as a one-time purchase. Cloud features are optional.
best_feature_set.rationale: Subscription fatigue is real ($10 to $30 a month across the category), and Pebble markets 'no subscription' as a feature. Processing locally makes this cheap to offer, and it also supports the privacy claims.

best_feature_set.feature: Session mode in the EU, UK and Germany
best_feature_set.description: Launch only after a DPIA and a review by local counsel on §201 StGB. Go first with wearer-only Memo mode and Sessions that require explicit consent, with EU data residency.
best_feature_set.rationale: The EDPB statement and German criminal law make ambient capture of bystanders in the EEA high-risk, and Limitless withdrew from the EU and UK. Apple's absence from the EU looks like an opening but is a trap for ambient capture.

best_feature_set.feature: Consented voiceprints for regular contacts
best_feature_set.description: A contact can be named automatically only after that person enrolls their own voice and gives explicit consent. They can revoke it at any time.
best_feature_set.rationale: Voiceprints of bystanders may count as GDPR Art. 9 biometric data. Named speakers are valuable, but only with the other person's consent.

best_feature_set.feature: Phone-call capture with a mandatory announcement
best_feature_set.description: Calls recorded on the iPhone, with an audible notice to all parties that cannot be turned off.
best_feature_set.rationale: Calls are the most heavily regulated recording context. Apple, Google and Truecaller have made announcing the recording the norm.
exemplars: Apple Voice Memos & Notes audio transcription (Apple Intelligence) (notifies all participants)

best_feature_set.feature: Team and workplace mode
best_feature_set.description: Admin recording policies, notice templates for employees, retention controls and legal hold, and redaction of material non-public information.
best_feature_set.rationale: Recording at work needs employer policy and notice. Enterprise buyers require governance.
exemplars: Webex AI Assistant (Cisco AI Assistant for Webex)

best_feature_set.feature: Modes for regulated professions
best_feature_set.description: Clinical, therapy and financial-advisor templates, with a BAA/HIPAA and consent workflows for clients.
best_feature_set.rationale: These are high-value markets, but each needs its own compliance.

best_feature_set.feature: Instant replay for watches without Live Rewind
best_feature_set.description: The watch keeps the last 15 to 30 seconds in RAM, and on request a clip goes to the iPhone for transcription. The app is honest about the latency.
best_feature_set.rationale: It helps accessibility and fills a gap Apple leaves on older watches. It needs a fast round trip to ASR, and the sync path today takes minutes.
exemplars: Apple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

best_feature_set.feature: Mac meeting capture without a bot, into the same vault
best_feature_set.description: Capture per-app audio on the Mac with Core Audio process taps, stored in the same vault and governed by the same consent rules.
best_feature_set.rationale: It covers the online half of the day, but it is a second product surface and does not affect the watch value.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 1. Start a Session with one tap, in the foreground
minimal_watch_set.description: The user taps once to start a long Session, optionally time-boxed. It keeps running with the wrist down and while the user opens other watch apps.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: watchOS only allows recording to start from a foreground user action and cannot restart it from the background. The tap is both the technical requirement and the legal and App Review basis. One-tap start is the most-loved watch feature, and continuing while the user uses other apps fixes a known Granola complaint.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: A WidgetKit complication or Smart Stack widget deep-links into the app, and the launch from that tap starts the Session immediately. A watchOS 26 Control (Control Center, Smart Stack, or the Action Button on Ultra) opens the app; it cannot start capture from the widget extension. An in-app Start button carries .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) for Double Tap (S9+ and SE 3; not in Low Power Mode). On start, activate AVAudioSession with category .record exactly once, install an AVAudioEngine input tap, and declare the 'audio' background mode. Do not bind the Crown double-press, which runs Live Rewind on Series 12 and Ultra 4. Do not depend on AudioRecordingIntent or Live Activities on the watch, whose behaviour there is unclear.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 2. Clear recording state and consent at the start
minimal_watch_set.description: A start chime plus haptic, a full-screen recording colour when the wrist is raised, a REC state with elapsed time on the complication, and a short consent card at the start of each Session in all-party-consent jurisdictions. The user records whether they announced it.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Guideline 2.5.14 requires clear indication and consent, and the EDPB says consent obtained after recording is invalid. A watch reads as a covert device, so the wearer has to be prompted to disclose. Without this the app is a liability, not a product.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: The system orange mic indicator appears automatically and cannot be hidden. Play the chime through the active audio session and a WatchKit haptic on start, stop, pause and resume. The chime cannot be turned off in Session mode. Onboarding stores the user's home jurisdiction; the default strict list is the 13 Kilpatrick states plus the EEA/UK. The consent card is a 2-second, non-blocking overlay. Write a consent flag (announced yes/no) into each segment's JSON sidecar so the iPhone can apply the matching retention policy.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 3. Instant Pause (bystander mode) and full Stop
minimal_watch_set.description: Pause immediately stops anything from being analysed or saved and can be resumed with the wrist down. Stop releases the microphone completely. The UI states plainly which one is active: 'Paused: mic open, nothing kept' or 'Stopped: mic off'.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Social settings are where people abandon these products (the Bee partner ban, a therapist's objection, Limitless users dropping social use). Limitless's own guidance is to turn the device off when someone declines. Pause has to be instant and reversible or people won't use it. Stop has to exist because the mic indicator stays lit while paused.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Pause flips a gate flag so the AVAudioEngine tap callback drops buffers before the VAD or the encoder sees them. The engine and session keep running, because re-activating from the background fails. The toggle is the large in-app button, Double Tap (.handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction)) and a complication tap. Stop deactivates the AVAudioSession; restarting then needs a foreground tap. After a configurable time paused (default 15 min), the app switches to Stop so it does not hold the mic indefinitely. Paused time is written as a GAP with reason 'user_pause'.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 4. Speech-gated capture in segments
minimal_watch_set.description: Only stretches that contain speech are encoded and saved. They go into 2-minute AAC segment files, each with a sidecar recording times, gaps, pauses, the consent flag and a hash.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: It keeps less third-party audio, uses less storage and fewer transfers, and makes data loss impossible to hide. Segments are what make sync and crash recovery reliable.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: The AVAudioEngine input tap feeds a ring buffer holding 3 to 5 seconds of pre-roll. A cheap energy threshold runs first; when it fires, the SoundAnalysis built-in classifier's speech class (watchOS 9+) confirms it. Confirmed audio is encoded as AAC mono, 16 kHz, 24 to 32 kbps; Opus on the watch is unverified. Each segment is flushed to disk every 2 minutes and recorded in a journal. On relaunch the app scans the journal and finalises any partial segment. Silence never reaches disk.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 5. Delivery ledger that never loses audio, with visible sync states
minimal_watch_set.description: A segment is deleted from the watch only after the iPhone confirms a durable write. The watch and complication show Recorded, Queued, On iPhone and Transcribed (for example, with a count of to-dos), so the user can see the result arrived without a separate review UI.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Lost or never-transferred recordings are complaint number one (Omi's 11 hours, Voice Memos truncation, Drafts after an update). A privacy-first brand has no second chance on trust.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Send each segment with WCSession.transferFile and metadata {id, seq, hash}, and track outstandingFileTransfers. The iPhone confirms with WCSession.transferUserInfo; sendMessage fails when the iPhone app is in the background. If the phone is unreachable, upload with a standard URLSession during the runtime the audio session already provides, to the user's encrypted endpoint; a background URLSession may wait for Wi-Fi. No sockets or WebSockets (TN3135, plus the reported ~36 to 38 s path-revocation bug). Keep segments to a few MB each. Test on hardware with the iPhone's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off; the Simulator does not support transferFile.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 6. Recovery after an interruption
minimal_watch_set.description: When a call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app ends capture, the open segment is closed with a reason. The user gets one haptic prompt, 'Recording stopped by call. Tap to resume', and summaries get an explicit gap.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: Capture stopping on interruption is complaint number two, and watchOS cannot resume it in the background. Without a prompt, users silently lose the rest of the meeting. Without GAP markers, summaries invent continuity.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: Observe AVAudioSession interruption and route-change notifications. Finalise the segment and write a GAP {start, end, reason}. Post one time-sensitive local notification with a haptic; its action opens the app in the foreground and calls the Session start path again. The complication switches to a 'Resume' state. Never loop notifications. The iPhone side passes GAP tokens to every summariser.

minimal_watch_set.feature: 7. Battery and storage limits, with an honest projection
minimal_watch_set.description: The app stops automatically before it can empty the watch or fill its storage, lowers quality in Low Power Mode, and shows hours remaining at the drain it has actually measured.
minimal_watch_set.why_essential: No public figure exists for continuous-recording drain (vendor claims range from 3 to 20 %/h), and Series 12 is rated at 24 h for everything. A watch dead by mid-afternoon fails at its main job, and inflated claims destroy trust.
minimal_watch_set.watchos_implementation: After each segment, check battery level and free space. Stop at 15% battery or below 100 MB free, then post a notification and finalise the segment. In Low Power Mode drop to 24 kbps; recording under Low Power Mode is untested, so validate it on hardware. Double Tap is unavailable in Low Power Mode, so keep the on-screen buttons. Record the drain per Session for each watch model and show '≈ X h left at this rate' in the app and on the complication. Make no public battery claim until it is measured on Series 9 and later, SE 3 and Ultra.

explicitly_cut.feature: Automatic, voice-triggered or scheduled auto-start (true ambient capture, wake word)
explicitly_cut.reason: The platform forbids it: capture must start from a foreground user action and cannot resume from the background. It is also the weakest legal position under all-party-consent laws and the EDPB statement. Schedules should only remind the user to tap.

explicitly_cut.feature: Hidden, silent or 'discreet' mode (no chime, dimmed state)
explicitly_cut.reason: The orange mic indicator cannot be hidden. Guideline 2.5.14 requires clear indication and 2.5.19 forbids hidden features, and the EDPB wants indicators hard to disable. A watch already looks covert, so this would make it a covert recorder.

explicitly_cut.feature: HKWorkoutSession or WKExtendedRuntimeSession keep-alives
explicitly_cut.reason: Developers report repeated rejections under 2.5.4/2.5.1 for this. A workout session also moves the user's Activity rings, and extended sessions are capped at 10 minutes to 1 hour. The audio background mode is the only legitimate path.

explicitly_cut.feature: On-watch transcription, live captions or on-watch LLM summaries
explicitly_cut.reason: watchOS has no Speech framework and no on-device LLM. PCC needs a managed entitlement, has daily quotas and requires a network connection, all at a battery cost. Transcription and summaries run on the iPhone.

explicitly_cut.feature: A clone of Live Rewind (instant text of the last 15 seconds)
explicitly_cut.reason: It needs a real-time round trip to ASR, but sync from the watch takes minutes and sockets are unreliable. On Series 12 and Ultra 4, Apple owns the Crown double-press. Moved to Later, with honest latency.

explicitly_cut.feature: Real-time streaming to the cloud over WebSockets or sockets
explicitly_cut.reason: TN3135 restricts low-level networking, and a path-revocation bug has been reported during audio sessions. Segment files with confirmations are more reliable and leave less third-party audio in transit.

explicitly_cut.feature: Naming other speakers or storing voiceprints of bystanders
explicitly_cut.reason: Bystander voiceprints may be GDPR Art. 9 biometric data, and naming people without consent breaks social trust. The minimal app separates only 'me' and 'others', on the iPhone, using the wearer's own enrolled voice.

explicitly_cut.feature: Phone-call capture
explicitly_cut.reason: Calls interrupt watch recording anyway, and they are the most regulated recording context, where the norms of Apple, Pixel and Truecaller require an announcement. Moved to Later on the iPhone with a mandatory notice.

explicitly_cut.feature: Proactive AI nudges and notifications on the watch
explicitly_cut.reason: Friend's unprompted texts and Omi's 'micromanager' critique show the backlash, and nudges cost battery and attention. The minimal app sends exactly one kind of notification: the resume prompt after an interruption.

explicitly_cut.feature: Agentic actions from the wrist (send email, create events, message people)
explicitly_cut.reason: The blast radius is large and approving actions on a small screen is hard. Actions stay on the iPhone, require explicit approval and come later.

explicitly_cut.feature: A highlight or bookmark gesture
explicitly_cut.reason: Double Tap supports one primary action and is reserved for Pause/Resume, which matters more socially. A bookmark is cheap to add later as an on-screen button.

explicitly_cut.feature: Ask-AI chat and memory search on the wrist
explicitly_cut.reason: It is a real unmet need, but it needs a phone round trip and system dictation, which stops after about 30 to 45 seconds. Deferred to the Differentiator tier; the minimal app shows only the Transcribed sync state.

explicitly_cut.feature: Sharing, links and team spaces
explicitly_cut.reason: Link sharing that defaults to 'anyone with the link' (reported for Granola by a secondary source) is a classic leak of third-party speech. There is no outbound sharing from the minimal app.

explicitly_cut.feature: Camera or visual context, location tagging and health-data fusion on the watch
explicitly_cut.reason: These widen the categories of data collected and the exposure of bystanders without adding capture value. Location is used later, only on the iPhone, for pause zones.

explicitly_cut.feature: Session mode in the EEA, UK or Germany at launch
explicitly_cut.reason: The EDPB statement, German §201 StGB criminal exposure and Limitless's withdrawal show the risk. Ship Memo mode (the wearer's own voice) first, and add Sessions only after a DPIA and legal review.

explicitly_cut.feature: Third-party cloud AI enabled by default
explicitly_cut.reason: Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires explicit permission, and the Otter suit alleges training on recordings. The minimal app is fully useful with on-device iPhone processing, and cloud is opt-in per provider.

proposals.architecture_notes:
POSITIONING. Position the product as an honest recorder for the watch people already own: user-started Sessions and Memos, never hidden 24/7 listening. Siri Recap and Live Rewind set the privacy bar (opt-in, chime, mic indicator, schedules and places, sensitive-data filters, 7-day deletion, E2E encryption) and are free. Compete where they stop:
- Series 9+ and SE 3 on watchOS 27, with a watchOS 26 fallback.
- iPhones without Apple Intelligence (Recap needs Series 12/Ultra 4 plus an iPhone 16 or later).
- Full transcripts with me/others labels.
- Retention the user chooses.
- More languages.
- Export and MCP.
- Recording that continues while the user opens other watch apps.
Match Apple's consent posture or beat it. Against Bee Frontier ($74.99, Alexa+), Plaud and Omi, the pitch is no extra device, a local-first vault, a no-subscription local tier and an exit guarantee (Limitless and Humane are the cautionary cases). Against Meta, Amazon and OpenAI (pendants and glasses arriving in 2027), the pitch is trust: no commerce or ad graph and no vendor copy by default. Only 76 of the 272 catalog products have consent controls and only 59 are local-only or E2E, so trust tooling is still open ground.

CAPTURE (WATCH).
1. A user tap in the foreground (complication, Control, Ultra Action Button, or Double Tap in the app) activates AVAudioSession(.record) exactly once and installs an AVAudioEngine input tap.
2. The 'audio' background mode keeps it running with the wrist down and while other apps are in use. An Apple Frameworks Engineer says recording continues in the background but cannot be resumed there.
3. Never stop the engine for silence or Pause. A gate drops buffers in RAM instead.
4. The pipeline runs: ring buffer with 3-5 s pre-roll, then an energy gate, then the SoundAnalysis built-in speech class, then AAC mono 16 kHz at 24-32 kbps, written as 2-minute segments with JSON sidecars (times, GAPs, pause and consent flags, hash) and a journal for crash recovery.
5. On an interruption (call, Siri, alarm, other audio): finalise the segment, write a GAP, send one time-sensitive 'Tap to resume' notification, and switch the complication to Resume.
6. Do not use HKWorkoutSession or extended-runtime sessions as keep-alives (2.5.4). Do not depend on AudioRecordingIntent or Live Activity behaviour on the watch. Leave the Crown double-press to Apple.

WHERE TRANSCRIPTION AND AI RUN. Nothing runs on the watch: there is no Speech framework and no SystemLanguageModel, and PCC needs a managed entitlement and has daily quotas. The iPhone companion is required:
- SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber (iOS 26) for long-form ASR.
- me/others separation using only the wearer's own enrolled voice.
- SoundAnalysis/ShazamKit to filter TV and music.
- On-device Foundation Models (4,096-token session context, 3-5 tools) for per-segment triage, action items and cited summaries.
An optional Mac node runs heavier diarization (FluidAudio or SpeakerKit with pyannote community-1; keep FluidAudio in a Swift 5.10 module) and WhisperKit for extra languages and custom vocabulary.

Cloud LLMs are opt-in for each provider (5.1.2(i)) and all traffic goes through one exit point that redacts or pseudonymises locally and logs every payload. Providers must offer zero retention and no training. Per the Earshot notes: claude-haiku-5-5 for bulk extraction, claude-opus-5-5 for daily synthesis, and Message Batches at 50% cost for nightly rollups. Use output_config.effort rather than thinking budgets and send no temperature, top_p or top_k. ClaudeForFoundationModels with .appAttest covers watchOS 27 and iOS without shipping a key, but cannot use the MCP connector or batch. Every derived object carries source_span_ids so it can cite its transcript span, and a coverage table backs honest 'not recorded' answers.

SYNC.
- Primary path: WCSession.transferFile for each segment with {id, seq, hash}. The watch tracks outstandingFileTransfers. The iPhone writes durably, then confirms over transferUserInfo, not sendMessage. The watch deletes a segment only after that confirmation.
- Fallback when the phone is unreachable: a standard URLSession upload to the user's own encrypted endpoint (CloudKit private database or self-hosted) during the runtime the audio session already provides. A background URLSession may wait for Wi-Fi.
- No sockets or WebSockets (TN3135; a ~36-38 s path revocation during audio sessions is reported as FB24377808).
- Expect minutes of latency. Show Recorded, Queued, On iPhone, Transcribed. Results come back to Smart Stack and complications through WidgetKit reloads.
- Test on hardware with the iPhone's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off.

PRIVACY DATA FLOW AND RECOMMENDED DEFAULTS.
- Watch: silence and paused audio are never written.
- Raw audio: encrypted on the iPhone for a 72-hour verification window (user can choose 0 h to 30 d, or pin a session), then crypto-shredded.
- Wearer's own transcript: kept until the user deletes it.
- Others' verbatim speech: 30 days where consent was logged or the jurisdiction allows. Otherwise, in the 13 Kilpatrick all-party states and the EEA/UK, it is reduced to a summary with no quotes. This lowers retention exposure but does not cure interception claims, so the announcement at the start of a Session is still the primary control.
- Sensitive-data filters (IDs, payment, auth, health, self-harm) run before storage and before anything leaves the device.
- Users can delete by time range or by session, which also serves bystander requests.
- Session mode is 18+.
- No vendor copy and no training by default.
- Publish the vault schema and an open-source reader.
- Distribute through TestFlight first and book Meet with Apple before App Store submission.

BATTERY BUDGET (all low confidence until measured). No rigorous public measurement exists, and vendor claims range from about 3%/h (Hedy) to 15-20%/h. The research brief's estimate from 100% to a 10-15% auto-stop is about 10-14 h on Series 11/12, 8-11 h on SE 3 and 18-24 h on Ultra 3, with Ultra 4 somewhat more. Design target: 5%/h or less on Series 9+ with the screen off. The mic and engine are always on; VAD saves encoder, storage and radio power, not mic power. No streaming. SoundAnalysis runs only after the energy gate fires. Transfers are batched.

Storage: 10.8-14.4 MB/h at 24-32 kbps, so a 16 h worst case is about 175-230 MB, and far less after speech gating, against 64 GB.

Limits: stop at 15% battery or under 100 MB free, and use 24 kbps in Low Power Mode (recording under Low Power Mode is untested). Promise 'a workday Session' publicly, never 'all day', and show measured projected hours in the app.

SOURCE CONFLICTS AND WHICH ONE I CHOSE.
1. App Review acceptance: the research brief says Apple never answered; the Earshot notes cite a specific rejection in forum thread 776949, where reviewers said audio background mode is for playback. I treat rejection as a real risk.
2. Siri Recap age limit: the Apple support doc says 18+ (primary source); the Earshot notes, via TechCrunch and Heise, say not for under-13s. I chose 18+ and apply it to Session mode.
3. Segment length: the brief recommends 1-5 min and Earshot 2 min. I chose 2 min.
4. Consent states: secondary sources say about 11-13. I chose Kilpatrick's 13-state list as the conservative default and treat Michigan as a hybrid per the brief; the statutes still need verifying.
5. Granola's watch app: one source says it must stay in the foreground, the other that it records wrist-down. Both fit: wrist-down works, opening another app stops it. Our differentiator is to keep recording in that case.
6. Stream Ring status and price: I preferred the Nov 16 catalog (shipping, Upstream $14.99/mo) over Earshot (preorder, $10/mo).
7. Pebble Index 01 price: the catalog says $75 rising to $99, Earshot says $99. It makes no difference to this analysis.
8. HKWorkoutSession: the sources cite guideline 2.5.4 and 2.5.1 respectively. Both say don't use it.
9. Bee requiring a button tap after the acquisition: single secondary source. The catalog still flags Bee as always-on, so I treat it as ambient-capable.
risks: App Review: a developer was rejected because reviewers said the audio background mode is for playback (forum 776949), and Apple has not said whether an all-day recording started by the user is acceptable. Mitigation: TestFlight first, book Meet with Apple, frame the feature as user-started, time-boxed Sessions with a chime and a visible state, use no keep-alive tricks, and never use the words 'always listening'.

Wiretap/CIPA litigation: Brewer v. Otter.ai (Aug 2025) and Subia v. Meta (Oct 2026) are verified, and Holland & Knight reports that early-2026 pleading-stage rulings mostly favoured plaintiffs on wiretap claims. The app vendor could be named alongside users. Discarding others' speech after capture limits retention exposure but does not cure interception claims in all-party-consent states. Chamberlain v. Granola rests on a single competitor blog and must not be cited externally.

EU and Germany: under EDPB Statement 01/2026, consent after recording is invalid, the household exemption is narrow and manufacturers cannot shift duties to users. German §201 StGB carries up to 3 years for unauthorised recording, and bystander voiceprints may be Art. 9 biometric data. Launching ambient Sessions in the EEA without a DPIA and local counsel is a legal and reputational risk; Limitless withdrew from the EU and UK.

Looks like a covert recorder: a watch shows no pendant-style LED to bystanders, and the orange mic dot is visible mostly to the wearer, so the product can read as covert. Social backlash drives churn and bad press: Bee was called the 'creepiest Apple Watch app', a Bee user's partner banned it, a therapist objected, and a long-term Limitless user stopped using it socially. The Announce and consent card features have to work in practice, not just exist.

Apple competing and controlling the platform: Siri Recap and Live Rewind are free, and Apple can widen them in any point release (languages, transcripts, older hardware, EU, a developer API). Apple also controls App Review, the mic indicator, gestures and background policy. Differentiators that rest on Apple's current gaps can vanish within a year. The durable ones are the user-owned vault, export, consent tooling and agent access.

Big-tech bundling and price pressure: Bee Frontier sells at $74.99 tied into Alexa+ and Prime. Meta has the Limitless team, a pendant in internal testing for spring 2027 and its Muse agent. Google's Intelligent Eyewear goes on sale Dec 10, 2026, and OpenAI and Apple glasses are expected in 2027. Compete on trust and ownership, not on price or model quality.

Data loss destroying trust: interrupted recordings cannot be resumed, transferFile is throttled (with one reported failure on a file under 30 MB), the network path is reportedly revoked about every 36 s during audio sessions, and recording under Low Power Mode is untested. Omi's 11-hour loss is still a top public complaint, and one viral loss incident would define the brand.

Unknown battery drain: if real drain is near the 15-20%/h end of vendor reports, Series and SE users get half-day Sessions and the core promise fails. Measure per model before making any claim, and auto-stop at 15%.

Harm from misattribution and hallucination: a summary that attributes words to the wrong person or invents a commitment can damage relationships or be misused as evidence. Siri Recap avoids speaker attribution entirely. Mitigation: cite transcript spans, label uncertainty, never share automatically.

Discovery, subpoena and breach exposure: stored transcripts of third parties are discoverable and attractive breach targets, and the TechCrunch op-ed raises evidentiary authentication. Minimisation, short audio windows, local-first storage, E2E encryption and no vendor copy all reduce what can be compelled or leaked.

Sensitive contexts: medical, therapy, legal privilege, schools, children as bystanders, and MNPI at work. Mitigation: default pause zones, Session mode limited to 18+ (matching Apple's age limit for Recap), and workplace policy templates. Expect employer bans in some workplaces.

Third-party AI disclosure: Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires naming third-party AI and getting explicit permission, and Otter is accused of training on recordings. A silent cloud call risks rejection and a lawsuit, so cloud must stay opt-in for each provider and go through one audited exit point.

Regulatory drift: California SB 1130, a mandate for capture indicators on wearables, passed both chambers and was vetoed on Sep 30, 2026, partly because it could cover smartwatches. Expect it to be reintroduced and design to an indicator mandate now.

Our own continuity: an acquisition or shutdown would repeat Limitless, which turned off capture and deleted regional data within two weeks. Unless the schema and an open-source reader are published and the product works locally without an account, the trust pitch is hollow.

Evidence quality: several inputs are single-source or unverified: Nirva's wearer-only isolation and Taya's voice suppression (both unshipped), Bee's switch to tap-to-record after the acquisition, Limitless's Consent Mode, the Granola lawsuit, and all continuous-recording battery figures. The catalog and the Earshot notes also disagree on Stream Ring and Pebble status and pricing. Re-verify before using any of these in external positioning.

critique.issue: The retention rules contradict each other. In strict jurisdictions with no logged consent, other people's words may not be kept verbatim in transcripts, yet raw audio of those same people is kept 72 h by default (the user can extend it to 30 days or pin a session indefinitely). That audio is more sensitive than the verbatim transcript being withheld. Also, 'Sensitive filters ... run before storage' cannot apply to audio: the audio has to be stored on the watch and the iPhone before anything can transcribe it, so the 72 h audio window keeps exactly the IDs, payment details and health talk the filters are meant to remove.
critique.fix: Make audio retention depend on jurisdiction and consent. Strict jurisdiction with no logged consent: shred the audio as soon as transcription succeeds (0 h), or keep only the spans attributed to the wearer, and turn off pinning. Elsewhere: 72 h. Reword the filters as 'run on transcripts and derived objects before they are saved, and before anything leaves the device'. When a filter flags a span, shred that span's audio immediately rather than at 72 h. Apply the same rule in the Core retention item, privacy_and_consent and sync_and_storage.

critique.issue: Silent stops are only detected while the app is alive to see them. Item 4 depends on AVAudioSession interruption and route-change notifications, but a crash, jetsam or system termination delivers no notification. After an interruption takes the audio session, the background runtime may end before the app has posted the time-sensitive notification and reloaded widgets. In those cases the user believes the whole day is being recorded, which the draft itself calls 'the worst failure possible'. Crash recovery at next launch only repairs the files; it does not tell the user.
critique.fix: Add a dead-man's-switch: at every 2-minute segment rotation, cancel and reschedule a local UNNotification for about 5 minutes later ('Recording stopped - tap to resume'). If rotations stop for any reason, the notification fires. On .began, post the resume notification before doing any file I/O. Have the complication show 'last saved hh:mm' so a stale REC state is visible. Add a soak test that kills the process and forces jetsam on device.

critique.issue: The minimal set has no way to act on an objection after something has been recorded. Pause and Stop only prevent future capture. The draft's own sources say consent obtained after recording is invalid (EDPB), and Limitless's guidance in the Earshot notes says to delete audio captured without consent. A bystander who says 'please delete that' can only be helped later on the phone, by which time the segments may already be transcribed.
critique.fix: Add a minimal-set control on the recording screen and complication: 'Discard last 5 min / 15 min / this Session'. It deletes the matching unsent segments on the watch and sends a tombstone {session, from, to} through transferUserInfo, which the iPhone applies before transcription or cloud egress, along with any derived objects. Write a GAP with reason user_discard and log it in the consent log.

critique.issue: The claim that the Session chime cannot be turned off is not supported by the implementation. Item 1 plays feedback with WKInterfaceDevice.current().play(.start). That plays a haptic whose sound follows the watch's silent mode, so the chime is silent when the watch is muted. Apple's Live Rewind can chime on silent because it is a system feature. The fallback ('.record with haptics only') explicitly drops the chime. The draft also cites Granola's chime that can't be turned off as a model to copy, but the Earshot notes list it as a Granola user complaint.
critique.fix: Choose one approach and gate it on a device test. Option A: play a bundled AVAudioPlayer clip under .playAndRecord and confirm on hardware that it plays in silent mode and with AirPods connected. Option B: drop the 'cannot be turned off' claim and rely on the orange indicator, the full-screen state, the haptic and Announce. Either way, mention the Granola complaint and offer a quieter chime in place of no chime.

critique.issue: Announce can play to the wrong listener, and .playAndRecord brings a routing risk. When AirPods or other Bluetooth headphones are connected, the pre-recorded notice plays into the wearer's ears, so the person it is meant for never hears it, yet the session logs announced=true. Bluetooth category options (HFP) can also move the input to the headset mic in the middle of a session, which changes what is captured. Even without headphones, the watch speaker is too quiet for a café table. Without Announce, .playAndRecord has little justification, since the brief's [H] path is .record.
critique.fix: Check AVAudioSession.currentRoute before Announce. If the output is not the built-in speaker, show an on-screen 'Tell people you're recording' card and log announced=false. Set category options without .allowBluetooth/HFP so input stays on the watch mic, and treat any input-route change as a GAP. If Announce is cut or kept only as an on-screen card, use .record.

critique.issue: The timed Pause resumes recording automatically after 15 minutes without the wearer confirming. That can quietly start recording again a person who asked not to be recorded, which undercuts the consent rationale the draft gives for Pause. A single haptic at the end of the timer is easy to miss.
critique.fix: When the timer ends, play a haptic and show 'Resume recording?', with Resume as the Double Tap target. Since the engine is still running, the gate flag can flip without re-activating the session; verify that a notification action can flip it from the background. Offer auto-resume only as an opt-in, and never as the default in strict jurisdictions.

critique.issue: Separating the wearer from other speakers is Core, and strict-jurisdiction retention depends on it, but the iPhone mechanism is never named or verified. The draft only says 'separate me from others against the wearer's own enrolled voice'. Its own risks list says diarization is verified only on the Mac (SpeakerKit needs macOS 14+), and the summary-only fallback depends on a confidence score nobody has defined.
critique.fix: Name a candidate for the iPhone: a Core ML speaker-embedding model, or a FluidAudio iOS build (verify), combined with the wrist-proximity energy cue. Define an acceptance gate on real wrist audio, for example wearer-attribution precision of at least 95% and the confidence threshold that triggers the fallback. Until the gate passes, strict-jurisdiction Sessions without consent store only summaries of non-wearer content. Label the feature 'Core, gated on spike'.

critique.issue: The vault's exit guarantee does not hold, and it conflicts with the tiering. Sync and reading rely on the CloudKit private database plus a 'published open-source reader'. A CloudKit container can only be reached by apps signed by the developer team that owns it, so a reader that someone else builds from source cannot read CloudKit data after a shutdown. The local read-only MCP server is 'run by the Mac vault reader', so a Core item needs a Mac app, while the architecture makes the iPhone the default node and puts the Mac companion in Later.
critique.fix: Base the exit guarantee on files: a scheduled, user-triggerable export of the documented JSON schema, Markdown and AAC files to Files or iCloud Drive, which any reader can parse. Then either move MCP to Later with the Mac companion, or put a minimal signed Mac reader explicitly in v1 scope and say so in the executive summary and tiering.

critique.issue: The battery claims are internally inconsistent. The ship gate of 6 %/h or less sits at the optimistic end of the brief's own estimate for Series 11/12 (10-14 h, i.e. about 6-9 %/h), and it is presented as attainable. The arithmetic is also off: a 12 h day at 6 %/h ends near 28%, not '20-25%'. The marketing line 'a workday Session on Series and SE models' contradicts the SE 3 estimate of about 8-11 h. None of this budgets the screen turning on at every wrist raise during a background session.
critique.fix: Set gates and claims per model. Series 11/12: gate ≤7 %/h, stretch goal 6 %/h. SE 3: promise 'most of a workday' or 'meetings', not a workday. Ultra: 'a full waking day'. Correct the end-of-day figure. Add measured screen-on cost per wrist raise to the budget, and publish no claims until measured.

critique.issue: The draft overlooks a UX consequence of the background audio session. The brief [H] says watchOS shows the app again whenever the wrist is raised. During a Session, the recording screen therefore replaces the watch face for hours. The draft relies on this for the bookmark ('raise plus pinch'), but the recording screen spec ('static colour state with elapsed time') shows no time of day. That damages the watch's main job and costs battery on every raise.
critique.fix: Design the recording screen as a stand-in for the watch face: current time prominent, elapsed time and state secondary, optionally the next calendar event. Verify on device whether the user can go back to their face and whether the setting to return to the clock applies. Measure the per-raise screen cost and include it in the battery budget.

critique.issue: The draft says nothing about data protection, a locked watch, or the watch being off the wrist. If segment files use complete protection, writes can fail once the watch locks off-wrist. Recording also carries on if the user takes the watch off and leaves it on a desk or charger. That captures rooms and people with no wearer present, which bystander-consent reasoning does not cover. Item 5 says Double Tap is unavailable wrist-down, but there is no off-wrist policy.
critique.fix: Write open segments with .completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication (or .completeUnlessOpen) and encrypt them at rest on the watch. Stop the Session with a GAP when batteryState changes to .charging, as a proxy for off-wrist. Add a device test that removes the watch, lets it lock, and checks that writes continue or stop cleanly as designed.

critique.issue: The crash-safety claim doesn't fit the file format. AAC written through AVAudioFile into an .m4a/MP4 container is unreadable until the file is closed, because the moov atom is written at close. 'At launch, finalise ... any orphaned segment' is therefore not possible for the open segment, so a crash loses up to 2 minutes. That is acceptable, but the draft describes it as recoverable.
critique.fix: Write segments as ADTS (.aac) or CAF, both of which tolerate a crash. The iPhone can transcode if it needs MP4. Otherwise state plainly that up to one segment (2 min) is lost on a crash, and consider 60 s segments.

critique.issue: Choosing the jurisdiction once at onboarding is fragile. Users travel, calls cross state lines (the Earshot notes say the strictest rule generally applies), and the 'conservative 13' list leaves out Michigan, which the brief lists as a hybrid. A user in a one-party state recording a visitor from California gets no consent reminder.
critique.fix: Show the 2-second consent reminder at the start of every Session, everywhere; it costs almost nothing. Use jurisdiction only to set retention and Announce defaults. Refresh coarse location from the iPhone at each Session start, and add MI and the other hybrid states to the strict set.

critique.issue: An essential preflight check is missing from the minimal set. Item 4's resume nudge needs Time Sensitive notification permission, capture needs mic permission, and transcription needs the companion app installed. If any of these is denied or missing, the honest-gap design fails silently, which is the failure the minimal set exists to prevent.
critique.fix: Add a preflight on the Start screen: mic permission, notification and Time Sensitive authorization, WCSession.isCompanionAppInstalled and reachability, free storage, and battery against projected hours. Show a blocking banner for anything missing; for example, if notifications are denied, show 'Interruptions won't alert you' and require the user to acknowledge it before starting.

critique.issue: The recap delivery and phone pipeline in Item 8 may not work. Once a Session ends, the watch app is no longer running, so updateApplicationContext doesn't reliably update it and widget reloads count against the budget. On the phone, transcription has no defined trigger: SpeechAnalyzer can't run for long during a short WatchConnectivity background wake. So 'Transcribed through hh:mm' and the evening recap may never arrive, bringing back the 'summaries never arrive' complaint.
critique.fix: Push the recap with transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo when a complication is on the active face. Use Text(timerInterval:) for elapsed time and reload only on state changes. On the iPhone, transcribe in a BGProcessingTask (while charging), when the app opens, and from a 'Process now' button, and show a 'Waiting for iPhone' state on the watch. Split Item 8 into status (essential) and recap (included if the phone pipeline is ready).

critique.issue: Some 'minimal' items are not essential to a recorder that actually works. Item 7 (the bookmark, with phone-side weighting) and the recap half of Item 8 depend on the full synthesis pipeline. The bookmark is also oversold: it can't answer 'what did they just say', because transcripts take minutes. The best_feature_set Core tier has 14 items, including routing to Things, Todoist and Notion, Ask over history, and MCP, which is beyond an MVP.
critique.fix: Mark Item 7 and the recap as 'v1 if cheap; cut first'. Remove the 'what did they just say' claim. Split Core into v1 and v1.x.

critique.issue: Several statements about Apple's features are wrong or overstated. The executive summary says Siri Recap and Live Rewind 'give summaries only', but Live Rewind shows the last 15 s as transcript text. 'Keep results for 7 days' and the market gap 'retention past 7 days' leave out that Recap summaries are kept if the user saves them.
critique.fix: Say that Recap gives summaries only and Live Rewind shows a 15-second transcript snippet. Say Recap summaries expire after 7 days unless saved. Reframe the gap as 'no full transcript, audio or export, and saving one summary at a time'.

critique.issue: Some catalog facts are misstated. Taya has not missed its date yet: its FAQ says 'Fall 2026', which is still current on Nov 16. iKairos missed a pre-order window, not a ship date. The Soundcore products don't fit 'about 300 free minutes' (Liberty 5 Pro Max has 120 min/mo; Soundcore Work lists no free tier). The list of push-to-talk rings includes Vocci, which flags always_on_capture and records up to 8 h continuously, and Natura, which hasn't shipped.
critique.fix: Replace Taya and iKairos with Pickle 1, IYO ONE and Plaud One Explorer (Q4 deliveries unconfirmed), or say 'are at risk of missing'. Drop Soundcore from the 300-minute pattern or write '120-600 free minutes'. Swap Vocci for WIZPR Ring or Stream Ring and note that Natura is unshipped.

critique.issue: The market_gaps line 'Only TicNote Watch sends results back' to the wrist is contradicted by the catalog: Siri Recap shows summaries on the watch, Pebble Time 2 shows Index 01 agent answers, Petey shows answers, and Granola taps the wrist before meetings.
critique.fix: Rephrase: 'No third-party Apple Watch recorder shows the day's capture coverage, gaps and top items on the wrist; Siri Recap shows summaries only on Series 12 and Ultra 4.'

critique.issue: There is a contradiction about Granola. The Differentiator states as fact that 'Granola's watch app stops when the user checks a text'. capture_strategy says the sources conflict and assumes background recording continues. The differentiator 'keep recording while the user glances at other apps' therefore rests on behaviour nobody has checked.
critique.fix: Mark the Granola claim as conflicting or unverified in the Differentiator, and make 'records while using other watch apps' depend on a device test before it appears in marketing.

critique.issue: The guidance on session activation is inconsistent. Item 1 says to call setActive(true) 'exactly once per session', but Item 4's Resume calls setActive(true) again after an interruption. The networking bug (FB24377808) is linked to repeated activation.
critique.fix: Reword to 'activate once per capture run (Start or user Resume); never re-activate during silence or Pause'. Note that each Resume is a new run, and test URLSession behaviour after a resume.

critique.issue: The delivery ledger is vague in places. 'Unreachable for N minutes' gives no value for N. 'Own HTTPS endpoint' is ambiguous next to the 'no vendor copy' claim. Nothing defines what counts as a receipt on the CloudKit path, or how the iPhone removes duplicates when a segment arrives by both paths.
critique.fix: Set N (for example 15 min). On the CloudKit path, treat CKModifyRecordsOperation success as the receipt. The iPhone de-duplicates by session, seq and sha256. Remove 'own HTTPS endpoint', or define it as an endpoint the user hosts.

critique.issue: The cloud-AI privacy claims conflict with the architecture. 'Providers must offer zero retention' sits alongside Message Batches for nightly rollups, whose results are stored server-side until retrieved, so ZDR eligibility needs checking. 'Use your own proxy' puts a relay the vendor runs in the data path, despite 'no vendor copy'. Bring-your-own-key users won't have a zero-retention agreement.
critique.fix: Confirm Batch ZDR eligibility with Anthropic, or state the retention window and drop Batches under the zero-retention promise. Specify that the proxy is stateless and logs no payloads, or prefer .appAttest. Show bring-your-own-key users a notice that the provider's retention terms apply.

critique.issue: The battery and storage APIs need verification. batteryLevel may be reported in coarse steps, so a %/h estimate at every 2-minute rotation will be noisy or zero for long stretches. volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey may not be available on watchOS.
critique.fix: Estimate drain by regression over a window of at least 30 minutes, and show 'measuring...' until then. Verify the resource key on watchOS and fall back to volumeAvailableCapacityKey.

critique.issue: The watchOS 26 fallback is underspecified. The draft targets Series 9 and later on watchOS 27 with a watchOS 26 fallback, but never says which models the fallback reaches (Series 6-8, SE 2, Ultra 1) or what they lose (Double Tap needs S9 or later; the older 32-bit builds). 'Older watches' is the headline gap against Apple.
critique.fix: State the device floor for the fallback, list the features lost on pre-S9 hardware (no Double Tap, so on-screen buttons only), and add Series 6-8 to the battery and soak test matrix, or narrow the 'older watches' claim to Series 9-11, SE 3 and Ultra 2-3.

critique.issue: The ring buffer may be too short for voice gating. A ~2 s ring buffer with 2 s pre-roll, behind an energy gate followed by a SoundAnalysis confirmation (about 1 s analysis window plus latency), can clip the first words of an utterance once confirmation delay is counted.
critique.fix: Size the ring buffer to at least 4 s, take pre-roll from the moment the energy gate trips rather than from SoundAnalysis confirmation, and check clipping on a labelled sample.

critique.issue: The Core consent item describes Session behaviour in the EEA, UK and Germany ('every Session shows a 2-second consent reminder'), while Session mode there is Later and launch is Memo-only.
critique.fix: In the Core item, say that in the EEA, UK and Germany only Memo mode ships at launch, and that the Session consent rules apply there once the DPIA-gated Later item ships.
